name: 前缀
title: Prefixes 小 and 第
explanation: A prefix is a small piece added to the front of a word. 小 (xiǎo, little/young) is put before a name or a family name as a friendly label, and 第 (dì, ordinal marker) goes before a number to turn it into an order word: 第 + number means first, second, third and so on.

name: 后缀
title: Suffixes 们 and 边
explanation: A suffix is a small piece added to the end of a word. 们 (men, plural marker) goes after a pronoun or a word for people to make a group: Person word + 们. 边 (bian, side) goes after a direction word to make a place word: Direction word + 边.

name: 名词
title: Position words
explanation: 上 (shàng, above/on), 下 (xià, below/under), 里 (lǐ, inside), 外 (wài, outside), 前 (qián, front) and 后 (hòu, back/behind) are nouns that tell where something is. They often follow a noun to say where it is in relation to that thing: Noun + position word.

name: 动词
title: Helper verbs 会 and 能
explanation: These verbs go before a main verb to say what someone is able to do: Subject + 会/能 + verb. 会 (huì, can/know how to) is for skills you have learned or for something likely to happen; 能 (néng, can/be able to) is for ability or for what circumstances allow.

name: 动词
title: Helper verbs 想 and 要
explanation: These verbs go before a main verb to express wishes: Subject + 想/要 + verb. 想 (xiǎng, would like to/want to) is a softer wish; 要 (yào, want to/going to/need to) is a stronger want, a need or a plan.

name: 动词
title: Helper verb 可以
explanation: 可以 (kěyǐ, may/can) goes before a main verb to say something is allowed or possible: Subject + 可以 + verb. It is the usual way to ask or give permission.

name: 动词
content: 看病、睡觉、说话、上课、下课、上班、下班、生病
title: Separable verbs
explanation: Words like 看病 (kànbìng, see a doctor), 睡觉 (shuìjiào, sleep), 说话 (shuōhuà, speak), 上课 (shàngkè, attend class), 下课 (xiàkè, finish class), 上班 (shàngbān, go to work), 下班 (xiàbān, finish work) and 生病 (shēngbìng, get sick) are verb + object packed into one word. Other words such as 了 (le, completed-action marker) can be inserted between the two parts, and the word cannot take a further object directly.

name: 代词
content: 多、多少、几、哪、哪儿、哪里、哪些、什么、谁、怎么、怎么样
title: Question words
explanation: These words stand in the spot of the thing being asked about, so the sentence keeps its normal word order and needs no 吗 (ma, yes/no question particle): 多 (duō, how, before an adjective), 多少 (duōshao, how many/how much), 几 (jǐ, how many, for small numbers), 哪 (nǎ, which), 哪儿 (nǎr, where), 哪里 (nǎlǐ, where), 哪些 (nǎxiē, which ones), 什么 (shénme, what), 谁 (shéi, who), 怎么 (zěnme, how/why) and 怎么样 (zěnmeyàng, how is it/how about it).

name: 代词
content: 我、你、您、他、她、我们、你们、他们、她们、它、它们、大家
title: Personal pronouns
explanation: These words stand in for people or things: 我 (wǒ, I), 你 (nǐ, you), 您 (nín, you, polite), 他 (tā, he), 她 (tā, she), 它 (tā, it), 我们 (wǒmen, we), 你们 (nǐmen, you all), 他们 (tāmen, they, male or mixed group), 她们 (tāmen, they, all female), 它们 (tāmen, they, for things or animals) and 大家 (dàjiā, everyone).

name: 代词
content: 这、那、这儿、那儿、这里、那里、这些、那些、有的、这个、那个、有些
title: Pointing words (this, that, some)
explanation: These words point to people, things or places: 这 (zhè, this), 那 (nà, that), 这个 (zhège, this one), 那个 (nàge, that one), 这些 (zhèxiē, these), 那些 (nàxiē, those), 这儿 (zhèr, here), 那儿 (nàr, there), 这里 (zhèlǐ, here), 那里 (nàlǐ, there), 有的 (yǒude, some) and 有些 (yǒuxiē, some). 这 and 那 are usually followed by a measure word and a noun: 这/那 + measure word + noun.

name: 数词
content: 一、二/两、三、四、五、六、七、八、九、零、十、百、半、千
title: Numbers
explanation: Basic numbers: 一 (yī, one), 二 (èr, two), 两 (liǎng, two), 三 (sān, three), 四 (sì, four), 五 (wǔ, five), 六 (liù, six), 七 (qī, seven), 八 (bā, eight), 九 (jiǔ, nine), 零 (líng, zero), 十 (shí, ten), 百 (bǎi, hundred), 半 (bàn, half) and 千 (qiān, thousand). Use 两 rather than 二 for two of something, before a measure word.

name: 量词
content: （1）专用名量词：本、个、家、口、块、件、只、元
title: Common measure words for nouns
explanation: Chinese puts a measure word between a number and a noun: Number + measure word + noun. Each measure word suits certain kinds of nouns: 本 (běn, for books), 个 (gè, the general all-purpose one), 家 (jiā, for families, shops, companies), 口 (kǒu, for family members), 块 (kuài, for pieces, and spoken word for money), 件 (jiàn, for clothes and matters), 只 (zhī, for animals) and 元 (yuán, yuan, the unit of money).

name: 量词
title: Container used as a measure word
explanation: 杯 (bēi, cup/glass) is a container word borrowed to count the amount of a drink: Number + 杯 + drink. It works like any measure word, but it names the container the drink is in.

name: 量词
title: Time and age measure words
explanation: These words count or name units of time and age, and they follow a number: Number + unit. 日 (rì, day of the month, written style), 号 (hào, day of the month, spoken style), 岁 (suì, years old), 点 (diǎn, o'clock), 分 (fēn, minute), 年 (nián, year) and 天 (tiān, day).

name: 副词
title: Degree adverbs
explanation: These words go before an adjective to say how strongly it applies: Subject + degree word + adjective. 非常 (fēicháng, extremely), 很 (hěn, very), 太 (tài, too/so), 真 (zhēn, really) and 有（一）点儿 (yǒu (yì) diǎnr, a bit, often for something unwelcome).

name: 副词
title: 都 meaning all
explanation: 都 (dōu, all/both) goes before the verb or adjective and says that everyone or everything in the group just mentioned is included: Plural subject + 都 + verb/adjective.

name: 副词
title: Actions in progress with 在 and 正在
explanation: 在 (zài, in the middle of) and 正在 (zhèngzài, right in the middle of) go before a verb to show that the action is happening now: Subject + 在/正在 + verb. This is different from 在 meaning at/in a place.

name: 副词
title: 再 for repeating later
explanation: 再 (zài, again/once more) goes before a verb to say an action will happen again or continue later: Subject + 再 + verb. It looks forward to a future repetition, not back to a past one.

name: 副词
title: Adding more with 还 and 也
explanation: These adverbs go before the verb and add something to what was already said. 也 (yě, also/too) says that another person or thing does the same; 还 (hái, in addition/also/still) adds something more or says a situation continues: Subject + 也/还 + verb.

name: 副词
title: Negation: 不, 没(有), 不要
explanation: These words go before a verb to make it negative: Subject + 不/没(有) + verb. 不 (bù, not) is for habits, the present and the future, and for adjectives; 没(有) (méi(yǒu), did not/have not/does not have) is for the past and for 有; 不要 (búyào, don't) tells someone not to do something.

name: 介词
title: 在 as at/in/on
explanation: 在 (zài, at/in/on) introduces the time or the place where an action happens: Subject + 在 + place/time + verb. It comes before the verb, not after it.

name: 介词
title: 和 and 对 introducing a person
explanation: These words introduce the other person involved in an action: Subject + 和/对 + person + verb. 和 (hé, with) means doing something together with someone; 对 (duì, to/toward) means the action is directed at someone.

name: 连词
title: 和 meaning and
explanation: 和 (hé, and) joins two or more words or phrases of the same kind, usually nouns or pronouns: A + 和 + B. It does not join whole sentences.

name: 助词
title: Describing with 的
explanation: 的 (de) links a describing word to the noun it describes, and shows possession: Possessor/description + 的 + noun. It is roughly like 's or like a describing phrase in English.

name: 助词
title: Completed action with 了
explanation: 了 (le) placed right after a verb shows the action has been completed: Subject + verb + 了 (+ object). It marks that something is done, not strictly that it is in the past.

name: 助词
title: Sentence-final particles 吧, 了, 吗, 呢
explanation: These small words come at the end of a sentence and add mood rather than content. 吧 (ba) softens a suggestion or guess, 了 (le) marks a change or completed situation, 吗 (ma) turns a statement into a yes/no question, and 呢 (ne) asks "what about...?", softens a question, or shows an action is still going on.

name: 叹词
title: Interjection 喂
explanation: 喂 (wèi, hello/hey) is an exclamation used to get someone's attention, especially when answering or starting a phone call. It stands outside the normal sentence structure and is usually followed by a comma or exclamation mark.

name: 结构类型
title: Coordinate phrases (items of equal rank)
explanation: Two or more words of the same kind are placed side by side as equals, such as noun + noun. They are often joined by 和 (hé, and) or simply set next to each other.

name: 结构类型
title: Modifier + head phrases
explanation: A describing word comes before the word it describes, giving the pattern Modifier + (的 (de, linking word)) + main word. In Chinese the describing part always comes first, as in adjective + noun.

name: 结构类型
title: Verb + object phrases
explanation: A verb is followed by the thing that receives the action, in the pattern Verb + object. The object comes after the verb, the same order as in English.

name: 结构类型
title: Subject + predicate phrases
explanation: A phrase made of a topic (who or what) followed by a comment about it, in the pattern Subject + predicate. It looks like a small complete sentence and can also sit inside a bigger sentence.

name: 结构类型
title: Number + measure word phrases
explanation: A number is followed by a measure word (a counting unit), in the pattern Number + measure word (+ noun). For example, 个 (gè) is the general measure word used when counting many kinds of things.

name: 结构类型
title: Preposition + noun phrases
explanation: A preposition (a small word showing relation) is followed by a noun or pronoun, in the pattern Preposition + noun. Common ones are 在 (zài, at/in) and 给 (gěi, to/for), and the whole phrase usually comes before the verb.

name: 结构类型
title: Location phrases
explanation: A noun is followed by a position word to say where something is, in the pattern Noun + position word. Examples are 上 (shàng, on/above) and 里 (lǐ, inside).

name: 主语
content: 名词、代词或名词性短语作主语
title: Subject
explanation: The subject is the person or thing a sentence is about, and it usually comes first. It can be a noun, a pronoun (a word that stands in for a noun, like "I" or "he"), or a noun phrase (a noun with describing words). Pattern: Subject + predicate (the part that says something about the subject).

name: 谓语
content: 名词、代词、数词或数量短语作谓语
title: Nouns, pronouns and numbers as the predicate
explanation: Sometimes the part that says something about the subject has no verb and is just a noun, a pronoun, a number, or a number plus measure word. This is common for stating things like age, date, time or price. Pattern: Subject + noun/pronoun/number phrase.

name: 谓语
content: 动词或动词性短语、形容词或形容词性短语作谓语
title: Verbs and adjectives as the predicate
explanation: The predicate is most often a verb or verb phrase (an action, with its objects and extra words) or an adjective or adjective phrase (a description, with no "to be" verb needed). Pattern: Subject + verb phrase, or Subject + adjective phrase.

name: 宾语
content: 名词、代词或名词性短语作宾语
title: Object
explanation: The object is the person or thing that receives the action, and it comes right after the verb. It can be a noun, a pronoun, or a noun phrase. Pattern: Subject + verb + object.

name: 定语
content: 名词性词语、形容词性短语、数量短语作定语
title: Words that describe a noun
explanation: A word or phrase placed before a noun to say which one or what kind is called a modifier. It can be a noun, an adjective phrase, or a number plus measure word. Pattern: Describing word/phrase (often with 的 (de, linking particle)) + noun.

name: 状语
content: 副词、形容词作状语表示时间、处所的词语作状语
title: Words that modify a verb or adjective
explanation: Adverbs, adjectives, and words for time or place can come before a verb or adjective to say how, when or where something happens. Time and place words go before the verb, not after it. Pattern: Subject + (time/place) + adverb/adjective + verb.

name: 补语
title: Verb + number of times
explanation: A number and a counting word for actions follow the verb to say how many times it happens. Pattern: Verb + number + action measure word, such as 次 (cì, time/occasion).

name: 句型
title: Sentences with a verb as the predicate
explanation: This is the basic sentence type where the main statement is a verb. Pattern: Subject + verb (+ object).

name: 句型
title: Sentences with an adjective as the predicate
explanation: The adjective itself says what the subject is like, with no "to be" verb such as 是 (shì, to be). Pattern: Subject + (很 (hěn, very)) + adjective, where a degree word like 很 often appears before the adjective.

name: 句型
title: Sentences with a noun as the predicate
explanation: The subject is followed directly by a noun or number phrase, with no verb "to be". It is typical for age, date, price, or origin. Pattern: Subject + noun/number phrase.

name: 句型
title: Sentences without a subject-and-comment split
explanation: These are short sentences that do not split into subject and predicate. They are single words or phrases that work on their own, such as greetings, calls, and exclamations.

name: 句类
title: Statements
explanation: A statement simply tells a fact, a thought, or a description. It has no question word or question particle, and it ends with a period.

name: 句类
title: Yes/no questions with 吗
explanation: A yes/no question asks whether something is true. Put 吗 (ma, question particle) at the end of a statement: Statement + 吗?

name: 句类
title: Questions with a question word
explanation: These questions use a word meaning who, what, where, and so on, such as 谁 (shéi, who), 什么 (shénme, what), or 哪儿 (nǎr, where). The question word goes in the spot where the answer would go, so the word order stays the same as in a statement.

name: 句类
title: Either-or questions with the verb repeated
explanation: Ask whether something is so or not by saying the verb or adjective, then 不 (bù, not), then the same word again. Pattern: Verb + 不 + verb, and the answer picks one of the two.

name: 句类
title: Commands and requests
explanation: These sentences tell or ask someone to do something. They often drop the subject 你 (nǐ, you) and may use 请 (qǐng, please) at the start, 不要 (bú yào, don't) for a ban, or 吧 (ba) at the end to soften the tone.

name: 句类
title: Exclamatory sentences
explanation: These sentences express strong feeling such as surprise, praise or complaint, and are usually written with an exclamation mark. They often use an intensifying word, as in 太 (tài, too, so) + adjective + 了 (le), or 真 (zhēn, really) + adjective.

name: 特殊句型
title: Sentences with 是 (equating or classifying)
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 是 (shì, to be) + noun. It says that the subject is the same as the noun, or belongs to the category the noun names.

name: 特殊句型
title: Sentences with 有 (possession)
explanation: Pattern: Owner + 有 (yǒu, to have) + thing owned. It says that someone or something has or possesses something. The negative uses 没有 (méiyǒu, does not have).

name: 特殊句型
title: Place + 是 + noun (what is at a location)
explanation: Pattern: Place + 是 (shì, to be) + noun. It tells you what is located at that place, and the noun is usually the thing that fills or makes up that spot.

name: 特殊句型
title: Place + 有 + quantity + noun (there is/are)
explanation: Pattern: Place + 有 (yǒu, to have; there is/are) + number + measure word + noun. It says that a certain amount of something exists at a place.

name: 特殊句型
content: （1）前后动作先后发生，后一动作是前一动作的目的
title: Two verbs in a row: second verb is the purpose
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb 1 (+ object) + verb 2 (+ object). One person does two actions in order, and the second action is the reason or goal of the first.

name: 特殊句型
content: （2）前一动作是后一动作的方式
title: Two verbs in a row: first verb is the method
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb 1 (+ object) + verb 2 (+ object). One person does both actions, and the first verb tells you the way or means by which the second action is done.

name: 特殊句型
title: Double-object sentences
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb + object 1 + object 2. The verb, such as one meaning give or tell, takes two objects in a row: first the person who receives, then the thing that is given or told.

name: 复句
title: Compound sentences without linking words
explanation: Two or more short clauses are placed side by side, usually separated by commas, with no connecting word between them. You work out the relationship (such as sequence, contrast or reason) from the meaning.

name: 复句
title: Adding a parallel fact with 也
explanation: Pattern: Clause 1, Subject + 也 (yě, also, too) + verb or adjective. The second clause adds something similar to the first, and 也 comes right before the verb or adjective.

name: 复句
title: Adding extra information with 还
explanation: Pattern: Clause 1, (Subject) + 还 (hái, also, in addition) + verb phrase. The second clause adds another action or fact on top of the first, and 还 comes before the verb.

title: Completed actions with 了
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb + 了 (le) + (number + measure word +) object. The particle 了 sits right after the verb and shows that the action has been completed.

title: Change of situation with sentence-final 了
explanation: Pattern: ... + 了 (le) at the end of the sentence. It shows that a new situation has appeared or something has changed, as in "now it is so" or "it has become so".

title: Ongoing actions with 在 / 正在
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 在 (zài, in the process of) or 正在 (zhèngzài, right in the middle of) + verb. It shows that the action is happening at this moment.

title: Ongoing actions with 在 / 正在 and 呢
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 在 (zài, in the process of) or 正在 (zhèngzài, right in the middle of) + verb (+ object) + 呢 (ne, a sentence-final particle). The 呢 at the end adds a relaxed tone and stresses that the action is going on now.

title: Ongoing actions with 呢 alone
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb (+ object) + 呢 (ne, a sentence-final particle), with no 在 before the verb. The 呢 alone can show that the action is in progress, and the context makes it clear.

name: 数的表达法
title: Expressing amounts of money
explanation: Pattern: number + 块 (kuài) or 元 (yuán, the basic unit, like a dollar) + number + 毛 (máo) or 角 (jiǎo, a tenth of the basic unit) + number + 分 (fēn, a hundredth). 块 and 毛 are used in speech, 元 and 角 in writing, and the last unit is often left off when speaking.

name: 数的表达法
title: Ordinal numbers with 第
explanation: Pattern: 第 (dì, ordinal prefix) + number (+ measure word) (+ noun). Putting 第 before a number turns it into an ordering word such as first, second or third.

name: 时间表示法
title: Dates and days of the week
explanation: Dates go from largest to smallest: number + 年 (nián, year) + number + 月 (yuè, month) + number + 号 (hào, day, spoken) or 日 (rì, day, written). The year is read digit by digit, and the weekday is 星期 (xīngqī, week) + number, with Sunday as 星期天 (xīngqītiān) or 星期日 (xīngqīrì).

name: 时间表示法
title: Telling the time
explanation: Pattern: number + 点 (diǎn, o'clock) + number + 分 (fēn, minute). Also look for 半 (bàn, half past), 刻 (kè, quarter of an hour) and 差 (chà, short of, to) for times before the hour; 2 o'clock uses 两 (liǎng, two) rather than 二.

name: 后缀
title: Suffix 面 for sides and directions
explanation: 面 (miàn, side, surface) is added after a position word such as 上 (shàng, up), 下 (xià, down) or 里 (lǐ, inside) to make a place word meaning that side or area. Pattern: Position word + 面.

name: 名词
title: Left and right
explanation: 左 (zuǒ, left) and 右 (yòu, right) are direction words, usually followed by 边 (biān, side) or 面 (miàn, side) to mean the left or right side. Pattern: 左/右 + 边/面.

name: 动词
title: Repeating a verb
explanation: Repeating a verb makes an action short, light or casual, like "do it a bit" or "have a go". The forms are AA (verb twice), A一A (verb + 一 (yī, one) + verb), A了A (verb + 了 (le, completed-action marker) + verb, for something already done), and ABAB (a two-character verb repeated as a whole).

name: 动词
title: 可能 for possibility
explanation: 可能 (kěnéng, may, might, possibly) is a helper verb that says something is likely but not certain. It goes before the main verb. Pattern: Subject + 可能 + verb.

name: 动词
title: Separable verbs
explanation: Some verbs are really a verb plus an object packed into one word: 帮忙 (bāngmáng, to help), 游泳 (yóuyǒng, to swim), 跳舞 (tiàowǔ, to dance) and 跑步 (pǎobù, to run). The two parts can be split by other words, and the verb can't take another object directly. Pattern: Verb part + (other words) + object part.

name: 代词
title: Asking why with 为什么
explanation: 为什么 (wèishénme, why) asks for a reason. It goes before the verb or at the start of the sentence, and the question needs no extra question word at the end. Pattern: Subject + 为什么 + verb?

name: 代词
title: 自己 for oneself
explanation: 自己 (zìjǐ, oneself, own) points back to the person who is the subject, or stresses that the person did something personally. Pattern: Subject + 自己 + verb, or Pronoun + 自己 for emphasis.

name: 代词
title: Pointing words for manner, degree and "every"
explanation: 这么 (zhème, this way, so) and 那么 (nàme, that way, so) go before an adjective or verb to show degree or manner. 这样 (zhèyàng, like this) and 那样 (nàyàng, like that) describe the way something is. 每 (měi, every, each) goes before a measure word. Pattern: 每 + measure word + noun.

name: 形容词
title: Repeating an adjective
explanation: Repeating an adjective makes the description more vivid or lively. A one-character adjective is doubled (AA), and a two-character adjective AB becomes AABB. The word often needs no 很 (hěn, very) in front and is usually followed by 的 (de, linking particle).

name: 数词
title: Numbers 万, 好多 and 多
explanation: 万 (wàn, ten thousand) is a number unit for counting in ten-thousands. 好多 (hǎoduō, a lot, many) is a vague amount. 多 (duō, more than, and a bit over) after a round number means slightly above it. Pattern: Number + 多 + measure word + noun.

name: 量词
title: Specific measure words
explanation: These measure words are used with particular kinds of nouns: 条 (tiáo, for long thin things like roads, rivers or fish), 位 (wèi, polite word for people), 间 (jiān, for rooms) and 名 (míng, for people with a role, such as students). Pattern: Number + measure word + noun.

name: 量词
title: Borrowed measure words
explanation: Some nouns can double as measure words by naming the container. 包 (bāo, bag, pack) counts things by the bag or packet. Pattern: Number + 包 + noun.

name: 量词
title: Counting actions with 次
explanation: 次 (cì, time, occurrence) counts how many times an action happens. It follows a number and comes after the verb. Pattern: Verb + number + 次.

name: 副词
title: Degree adverbs 多, 好 and 最
explanation: These words go before an adjective to show how much. 多 (duō, how, so) asks "how...?" or exclaims "how...!", 好 (hǎo, very, so) strengthens the adjective, and 最 (zuì, most) gives the highest degree. Pattern: Degree word + adjective.

name: 副词
title: Doing things together with 一起
explanation: 一起 (yìqǐ, together) goes before the verb to show people do something with each other. Pattern: Subject + 一起 + verb.

name: 副词
content: 还2、已经、有时（候）、快、快要、正
title: Time adverbs
explanation: These words go before the verb to show timing: 还 (hái, still), 已经 (yǐjīng, already), 有时（候） (yǒushí or yǒushíhou, sometimes), 快 (kuài, soon) and 快要 (kuàiyào, about to), and 正 (zhèng, in the middle of doing). 快 and 快要 are often paired with 了 (le, change-of-state particle) at the end. Pattern: Subject + time adverb + verb.

name: 副词
title: Frequency adverbs 常 and 经常
explanation: 常 (cháng, often) and 经常 (jīngcháng, often, frequently) say that something happens again and again. They go before the verb. Pattern: Subject + 常/经常 + verb.

name: 副词
title: Telling someone not to, with 别
explanation: 别 (bié, don't) is used to tell someone not to do something. It goes before the verb. Pattern: 别 + verb.

name: 副词
title: Linking adverbs 再 and 就
explanation: 再 (zài, again, then) and 就 (jiù, then, right away) connect two actions in order. 再 means one thing happens again or later, after the first, and 就 means the next thing follows soon or immediately. Pattern: First action + 再/就 + next action.

name: 副词
title: Adverbs of emphasis: 都, 就, 还是
explanation: These adverbs sit before the verb or adjective and add the speaker's attitude. 都 (dōu) here means "already" or "even", 就 (jiù) stresses "exactly", "just" or "right away", and 还是 (háishi) means "had better" or "still".

name: 介词
title: 从 for starting time or place
explanation: 从 (cóng, from) marks where or when something starts. Pattern: Subject + 从 + time/place + verb.

name: 介词
title: 往 for direction
explanation: 往 (wǎng, toward) shows the direction of a movement. Pattern: Subject + 往 + direction/place + verb.

name: 介词
title: 从 for a route
explanation: Here 从 (cóng, through, along, by way of) names the path a movement takes. Pattern: Subject + 从 + place passed through + verb of movement.

name: 介词
title: 给 for the receiver
explanation: 给 (gěi, to, for) introduces the person who receives or benefits from an action. Pattern: Subject + 给 + person + verb.

name: 介词
title: Comparison with 比
explanation: 比 (bǐ, than, compared with) sets two things side by side. Pattern: A + 比 + B + adjective, meaning A is more of that quality than B.

name: 介词
title: 跟 meaning "with"
explanation: 跟 (gēn, with) introduces the person you do something with or toward. Pattern: Subject + 跟 + person + verb.

name: 介词
title: 因为 before a noun or short phrase
explanation: 因为 (yīnwèi, because of) introduces the cause of something, usually followed by a noun or short phrase. Pattern: 因为 + reason, result.

name: 连词
title: 跟 meaning "and"
explanation: Here 跟 (gēn, and) joins two nouns or phrases of the same kind, like a plain "and". Pattern: A + 跟 + B.

name: 连词
content: 但、但是、那、虽然、还是2、因为2、所以
title: Conjunctions linking clauses
explanation: These words link two clauses or sentences: 但 (dàn, but) and 但是 (dànshì, but) mark contrast, 虽然 (suīrán, although) sets up a contrast, 因为 (yīnwèi, because) gives a reason and 所以 (suǒyǐ, so) gives the result. 那 (nà, in that case) draws a conclusion, and 还是 (háishi, or) offers a choice. Common pairs: 虽然……但是……, 因为……所以…….

name: 助词
title: Particles 得 and 地
explanation: Both are pronounced de and link a word to a description. 得 (de) goes after a verb or adjective and introduces how well or to what degree: Verb + 得 + description. 地 (de) goes after a descriptive word and before the verb: Description + 地 + verb.

name: 助词
title: Past experience with 过
explanation: 过 (guo) comes right after a verb to say someone has done it at some time before. Pattern: Subject + verb + 过 + object. Its negative uses 没 (méi, not) before the verb.

name: 助词
title: Continuing state with 着
explanation: 着 (zhe) comes right after a verb to show an action or state that is continuing. Pattern: Subject + verb + 着 (+ object).

name: 助词
title: Sentence-ending particles 呢, 吧, 的, 啊
explanation: These small words at the end of a sentence add tone. 呢 (ne) suggests something is still going on or adds liveliness, 吧 (ba) softens a suggestion or a guess, 的 (de) states something as certain, and 啊 (a) adds warmth or exclamation. They have no meaning of their own to translate.

name: 结构类型
title: Verb + complement
explanation: A verb can be followed by a complement, an added word that tells the result, direction or degree of the action. Pattern: Verb + complement.

name: 结构类型
title: Phrases ending in 的
explanation: A word or phrase plus 的 (de) can stand in for a noun, meaning "the one(s) that is/are...", when the noun is clear from context. Pattern: Description + 的.

name: 结构类型
title: Verbs in a series
explanation: One subject is followed by two or more verb phrases with no linking word. They show actions in order, or one action as the way or purpose of the other. Pattern: Subject + verb phrase 1 + verb phrase 2.

name: 结构类型
title: Pivot phrases
explanation: One person is both the object of the first verb and the subject of the second verb. Pattern: Subject + verb 1 + person + verb 2, as with 请 (qǐng, invite, ask) or 让 (ràng, let, make).

name: 功能类型
title: Noun phrases
explanation: A noun phrase is a group of words that works as a noun, such as a noun with descriptive words before it. It can be the subject or object of a sentence.

name: 功能类型
title: Verb phrases
explanation: A verb phrase is a group of words built around a verb, such as a verb with its object, an adverb or a complement. It usually acts as the predicate, the part saying what the subject does.

name: 功能类型
title: Adjective phrases
explanation: An adjective phrase is a group of words built around an adjective, often with a degree word before it. It describes a person or thing or serves as the predicate.

name: 固定短语
title: 什么的 meaning "and so on"
explanation: 什么的 (shénme de, and so on, and the like) comes at the end of a list of things to show the list is not complete. Pattern: A、B、C + 什么的.

title: Suggesting with 还是……吧
explanation: This pair makes a suggestion that something is the better choice. Pattern: Subject + 还是 (háishi, had better) + verb phrase + 吧 (ba, softening suggestion).

title: About to happen: 要/快要/就要……了
explanation: These patterns say something will happen very soon. Pattern: Subject + 要 (yào, be about to) / 快要 (kuàiyào, be just about to) / 就要 (jiùyào, be about to any moment now) + verb + 了 (le, marks a new situation).

title: Already with 都……了
explanation: Here 都 (dōu, already) works with 了 (le, marks a new situation) to say that something has already happened or reached a point, often later or further than expected. Pattern: Subject + 都 + verb/time/amount + 了.

name: 主语
title: Receiver of the action as subject
explanation: Sometimes the subject is not the one doing the action but the thing the action happens to, and the doer is often not mentioned. Pattern: Receiver (subject) + verb phrase. English usually translates it with a passive, such as "was finished" or "has been sold".

name: 谓语
title: Noun phrase as the predicate
explanation: The predicate is the part that says something about the subject. Here it is just a noun or number phrase, with no 是 (shì, to be) or other verb. Pattern: Subject + noun/number phrase. It is common for age, dates, prices and origin.

name: 定语
content: 动词或动词性短语、主谓短语作定语
title: Verbs and clauses describing a noun
explanation: A verb, a verb phrase or a whole subject-plus-verb clause can come before a noun to describe it, usually linked by 的 (de, the particle joining a describing part to its noun). Pattern: Verb phrase or Subject + verb + 的 + noun. Read it like an English relative clause: "the noun that …".

name: 补语
title: Result complements 错, 懂, 好, 会, 完
explanation: A word added right after a verb tells the result of the action. Pattern: Verb + result word. The result words are 错 (cuò, wrong), 懂 (dǒng, understand), 好 (hǎo, done properly or well), 会 (huì, have learned how) and 完 (wán, finish).

name: 补语
content: 简单趋向补语的趋向意义用法：（1）动词+来/去
title: Direction complements 来 and 去
explanation: After a verb of movement, 来 (lái, come) shows the movement is toward the speaker or the point of view, and 去 (qù, go) shows it is away from it. Pattern: Verb + 来/去.

name: 补语
title: Direction complements 上, 下, 进, 出, 过, 回
explanation: These words after a verb show which way something moves: 上 (shàng, up), 下 (xià, down), 进 (jìn, in), 出 (chū, out), 过 (guò, across or past) and 回 (huí, back). Pattern: Verb + direction word.

name: 补语
content: 复合趋向补语的趋向意义用法：动词+出来/出去/过来/过去/回来/回去/进来/进去/起来/上来/上去/下来/下去
title: Compound direction complements
explanation: A direction word and 来 (lái, come) or 去 (qù, go) are combined after a verb to show direction of movement and whether it is toward or away from the speaker. The forms are 出来 (chūlái, out toward), 出去 (chūqù, out away), 过来 (guòlái, over toward), 过去 (guòqù, over away), 回来 (huílái, back toward), 回去 (huíqù, back away), 进来 (jìnlái, in toward), 进去 (jìnqù, in away), 起来 (qǐlái, up), 上来 (shànglái, up toward), 上去 (shàngqù, up away), 下来 (xiàlái, down toward) and 下去 (xiàqù, down away). Pattern: Verb + compound direction word.

name: 补语
title: Complement of manner with 得
explanation: The particle 得 (de) after a verb introduces a description of how well, how fast or to what degree the action is done. Pattern: Subject + verb + 得 + adjective phrase. The adjective phrase often has a degree word, like 很 (hěn, very).

name: 补语
title: Duration of an action
explanation: A length of time placed after a verb says how long the action lasts. Pattern: Subject + verb + length of time. If the verb also has an object, the time phrase usually goes after the verb, either before the object or after the verb is repeated with the object.

name: 补语
title: Adjective followed by an amount
explanation: An amount placed after an adjective says how much the quality differs or changes, for example by a certain number of units or by 一点儿 (yìdiǎnr, a little). Pattern: Adjective + amount. It is often used with comparisons or changes.

name: 句型
title: Sentence whose predicate has its own subject
explanation: The predicate of the sentence is itself a subject plus predicate. The first subject is the overall topic, and the second names a part or aspect of it. Pattern: Topic + (Subject 2 + description). In English it reads like "As for the topic, its aspect is …".

name: 句类
content: 用“还是”连接的选择问句
title: Choice questions with 还是
explanation: 还是 (háishi, or) joins two options and asks the listener to pick one. Pattern: Option A + 还是 + Option B. It does not need 吗 (ma, the yes/no question particle).

name: 句类
title: Commands with 别
explanation: 别 (bié, don't) before a verb tells someone not to do something. Pattern: 别 + verb (+ object). It is a negative command or a request to stop.

name: 特殊句式
title: 是 sentences that describe or characterize
explanation: 是 (shì, to be) can link a subject to a description of its nature, type or characteristics, not just to a name or identity. Pattern: Subject + 是 + phrase describing it. English often translates it as "is" or "is a kind of".

name: 特殊句式
title: 有 meaning "reach" or "amount to"
explanation: 有 (yǒu, to have) can mean that something reaches a certain amount, such as height, weight or age, rather than owning something. Pattern: Subject + 有 + amount (+ measure or description).

name: 特殊句式
content: 处所+动词+着(+数量短语)+名词
title: Describing what is at a place with 着
explanation: This pattern says what is there in a place, in a state that continues, using 着 (zhe, a particle for a continuing state). Pattern: Place + verb + 着 (+ number + measure word) + noun. The place comes first, and the thing found there comes last.

name: 特殊句式
title: Comparison with 比
explanation: 比 (bǐ, compared with) places two things side by side to say that A has more of a quality than B. Pattern: A + 比 + B + adjective. The adjective normally stands alone, without a degree word like 很 (hěn, very).

name: 特殊句式
content: （2）A比B+形容词+数量补语/程度补语
title: Comparison with 比 plus how much more
explanation: After the adjective in a 比 (bǐ, compared with) comparison, you can add an amount or a degree word to say how big the difference is. Pattern: A + 比 + B + adjective + amount (such as a number with a measure word, or 一点儿 yìdiǎnr, a little) or degree word (such as 多 duō, much).

name: 特殊句式
title: Comparison with 有 and 没有
explanation: 有 (yǒu, to have) here means A reaches the level of B, and 没有 (méiyǒu, not have) means A does not reach it. Pattern: A + 有/没有 + B (+ 这么/那么) + adjective. 这么 (zhème, this/so) and 那么 (nàme, that/so) are optional and add the sense of "so" or "that".

name: 特殊句式
content: （4）A比B+动词+得+形容词/A+动词+得+比+B+形容词
title: Comparing how actions are done
explanation: This compares how well or how much two people do an action, using 得 (de, linking the verb to its description) and 比 (bǐ, compared with). Patterns: A + 比 + B + verb + 得 + adjective, or A + verb + 得 + 比 + B + adjective. Both mean A does it more than B.

name: 特殊句式
content: 强调时间、地点、方式、动作者
title: 是……的 to stress details of a past event
explanation: 是 (shì, to be) and 的 (de, a sentence-ending particle here) surround a detail to emphasize it, usually when the action has already happened. Pattern: Subject + 是 + time/place/manner/doer + verb + 的. The emphasized detail sits right after 是, and 是 is sometimes left out.

name: 特殊句式
content: 表使令：主语+请/叫/让……+宾语1+动词+宾语2
title: Causing someone to act: 请, 叫, 让
explanation: These verbs make or ask another person do something: 请 (qǐng, invite or ask politely), 叫 (jiào, tell or order) and 让 (ràng, let or make). Pattern: Subject + 请/叫/让 + person + verb + object. The person is both the object of the first verb and the doer of the second.

name: 特殊句式
title: Giving with 给 and two objects
explanation: After a verb of giving or passing on, 给 (gěi, to give) leads to the recipient and then the thing given. Pattern: Subject + verb + 给 + recipient + thing. The first object is the person who receives, and the second is the item.

name: 复句
title: Either … or … with （是）…还是…
explanation: This offers two possibilities inside one sentence. Pattern: (是) + Option A, 还是 + Option B. 是 (shì, to be) is optional, and 还是 (háishi, or) introduces the second option, often in a question or a statement about choosing.

name: 复句
title: Although … but … with 虽然 and 但是
explanation: This links two contrasting ideas. Pattern: 虽然 (suīrán, although) + Clause 1, 但是 (dànshì, but) + Clause 2. The second clause gives the contrasting point, which is the one the speaker stresses.

name: 复句
title: Cause and result with 因为……所以……
explanation: Pattern: 因为 (yīnwèi, because) + reason clause, 所以 (suǒyǐ, so) + result clause. The two words work as a pair linking a reason to its result, though one of them is sometimes left out.

name: 复句
title: "As soon as" with 一……就……
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 一 (yī, once) + verb, 就 (jiù, then) + second verb. It says that the second action follows right after the first one, as in "as soon as A happens, B happens."

content: 动词+着：（1）表示状态的持续
title: Verb + 着: a continuing state
explanation: Pattern: Verb + 着 (zhe, a particle marking something that continues). Here it shows that a state, such as a position or a condition left by an earlier action, stays in place.

title: Verb + 着: an ongoing action
explanation: Pattern: Verb + 着 (zhe, a particle marking something that continues). Here it shows an action that is still going on, often as the way or manner in which a second verb happens.

title: Past experience with 过
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb + 过 (guo, have done before). It says someone has had that experience at some point in the past. The negative uses 没 (méi, not) before the verb, with 过 kept after it.

name: 数的表达法
title: Order expressed by number + measure word
explanation: Pattern: Number + measure word (+ noun). Without the usual ordinal marker 第 (dì, the prefix that makes a number mean "nth"), a number followed directly by a measure word such as 号 (hào, number or day of the month) or 楼 (lóu, floor) gives a position in a sequence.

name: 数的表达法
content: 概数表达法1：（1）用“几”表示概数
title: Approximate numbers with 几
explanation: In a statement, 几 (jǐ, a few, several) stands for a small, unspecified number, usually under ten. Pattern: 几 + measure word + noun. It looks like the question word "how many," but here it is not asking anything.

name: 数的表达法
title: "More than" with number + 多 + measure word
explanation: Pattern: Number + 多 (duō, more than) + measure word + noun. The number is usually a round one such as ten or a hundred, and 多 comes right after it to say a bit more than that.

name: 数的表达法
title: "More than" with number + measure word + 多
explanation: Pattern: Number + measure word + 多 (duō, more than) + noun. Here 多 comes after the measure word and says there is a little extra beyond the stated amount.

name: 前缀
title: The prefix 老
explanation: 老 (lǎo, old) goes before a surname or certain relationship and job words to make them sound familiar or friendly. In this use it does not necessarily mean "old."

name: 后缀
title: Suffixes 家, 子 and 员
explanation: These endings attach to the end of a word to build nouns for people or things. 家 (jiā) marks an expert or specialist in a field, 子 (zi, a neutral-tone noun ending with little meaning of its own) marks a noun, and 员 (yuán) marks a member or worker in a role.

name: 名词
content: 东、南、西、北、北方、东方、南方、西方、中间
title: Direction and position nouns
explanation: These nouns name directions or places: 东 (dōng, east), 南 (nán, south), 西 (xī, west), 北 (běi, north), 北方 (běifāng, the north), 东方 (dōngfāng, the east), 南方 (nánfāng, the south), 西方 (xīfāng, the west) and 中间 (zhōngjiān, middle). They can name a place by themselves or come before another noun to describe it.

name: 动词
title: Modal verbs of need, duty and willingness
explanation: Pattern: Subject + modal verb + main verb. The modal verbs are 需要 (xūyào, need to), 该 (gāi, should), 应该 (yīnggāi, should or ought to), 愿意 (yuànyì, be willing to) and 得 (děi, must or have to). Read 得 as děi when it comes before a verb in this sense.

name: 动词
content: 动宾式离合词：放假、见面、结婚、洗澡
title: Verb-object separable words
explanation: Words such as 放假 (fàngjià, have a holiday), 见面 (jiànmiàn, meet), 结婚 (jiéhūn, get married) and 洗澡 (xǐzǎo, take a bath) are built from a verb plus an object. Other elements can be inserted between the two parts, and they cannot take another object directly.

name: 动词
content: 动补式离合词：离开、完成、分开
title: Verb-result separable words
explanation: Words such as 离开 (líkāi, leave), 完成 (wánchéng, complete) and 分开 (fēnkāi, separate) are made of a verb plus a result. Small words like 得 (de) or 不 (bù, not) can be inserted between the two parts to say something can or cannot be done.

name: 代词
title: "How" with 怎样
explanation: 怎样 (zěnyàng, how, in what way) is a question word that asks about manner or condition. Pattern: Subject + 怎样 + verb, or Subject + 怎样 on its own to ask what something is like.

name: 代词
content: 疑问代词的非疑问用法：（1）任指用法：①疑问代词+都……②疑问代词+疑问代词
title: Question words meaning "any" or "whoever"
explanation: A question word can be used without asking a question. With 都 (dōu, all): question word + 都 + ..., it means "every" or "any," with no exceptions. When the same question word appears twice in a sentence, the second one points back to the first, as in "whoever... that person."

name: 代词
title: Question words meaning "some" or "someone"
explanation: In a statement, a question word can stand for an unspecified person, thing, place or time, like "someone," "something" or "somewhere." It is used when the speaker does not know or does not need to say exactly which one, and it does not ask a question.

name: 代词
title: Pronouns 别人 and 咱们
explanation: 别人 (biérén, other people, others) refers to people other than the speaker or the person already mentioned. 咱们 (zánmen, we or us) includes the listener, unlike 我们 (wǒmen, we), which may leave the listener out.

name: 代词
title: "Other" and "else" with 别的 and 其他
explanation: 别的 (biéde, other, else) and 其他 (qítā, other, the rest) point to things or people besides the ones just mentioned. They can come before a noun or stand alone in place of one.

name: 量词
content: （1）专用名量词：把、双、张、种、层、封、页、辆、节、所、班、段、头、句公斤、斤、角、毛、刻、米
title: Common measure words for nouns
explanation: Pattern: Number or 这/那 (zhè/nà, this/that) + measure word + noun. The measure words in this group are 把 (bǎ, for things with a handle), 双 (shuāng, pair), 张 (zhāng, flat things), 种 (zhǒng, kind), 层 (céng, floor or layer), 封 (fēng, letter), 页 (yè, page), 辆 (liàng, vehicle), 节 (jié, class period or section), 所 (suǒ, buildings like schools or hospitals), 班 (bān, class or scheduled run), 段 (duàn, section), 头 (tóu, large animals like cattle), 句 (jù, sentence), 公斤 (gōngjīn, kilogram), 斤 (jīn, half kilogram), 角 (jiǎo, a tenth of a yuan), 毛 (máo, spoken form of 角), 刻 (kè, quarter hour) and 米 (mǐ, meter).

name: 量词
title: Containers used as measure words
explanation: Pattern: Number + container word + noun. 碗 (wǎn, bowl) and 盘 (pán, plate) are ordinary nouns borrowed to measure an amount, meaning a bowlful or a plateful of something.

name: 量词
title: Measure words for actions
explanation: Pattern: Verb + number + measure word. These words count how many times an action happens: 口 (kǒu, mouthful or bite), 回 (huí, occurrence or time), 遍 (biàn, one full time through from start to finish) and 声 (shēng, a sound or call).

name: 量词
title: Doubled measure words
explanation: Repeating a measure word, as in 个个 (gègè, every single one) and 张张 (zhāngzhāng, every single flat item), means "each and every." It is often followed by 都 (dōu, all) and describes all members of a group without exception.

name: 副词
content: 比较、还3、更、特别、挺、有些、越、极
title: Degree adverbs
explanation: These words go before an adjective to show how much: 比较 (bǐjiào, relatively), 还 (hái, even more, used in comparisons), 更 (gèng, even more), 特别 (tèbié, especially), 挺 (tǐng, quite), 有些 (yǒuxiē, somewhat), 越 (yuè, more and more, often paired as "the more... the more...") and 极 (jí, extremely).

name: 副词
content: 就3、一块儿、一共、只、到处、只是
title: Scope adverbs (only, together, altogether)
explanation: These adverbs say how much or how widely something applies, and they go before the verb: Subject + adverb + verb. They are 就 (jiù, only, just), 一块儿 (yíkuàir, together), 一共 (yígòng, altogether, in total), 只 (zhǐ, only), 到处 (dàochù, everywhere) and 只是 (zhǐshì, only, just).

name: 副词
content: 才1、马上、先、一会儿、刚、刚刚、一直
title: Time adverbs (just, first, right away)
explanation: These adverbs say when or in what order something happens, and they sit before the verb. They are 才 (cái, only just, not until), 马上 (mǎshàng, right away), 先 (xiān, first), 一会儿 (yíhuìr, in a moment), 刚 (gāng, just now), 刚刚 (gānggāng, just now) and 一直 (yìzhí, all along, continuously). Here 才 suggests something happens later than expected.

name: 副词
title: Frequency adverbs (always, often, again)
explanation: These adverbs say how often an action happens, and they go before the verb. They are 总 (zǒng, always), 总是 (zǒngshì, always), 又 (yòu, again, for something that has already happened) and 常常 (chángcháng, often).

name: 副词
title: Doing two things at once with 一边
explanation: 一边 (yìbiān, at the same time) shows two actions going on together. The pattern is Subject + 一边 + verb 1 + 一边 + verb 2, meaning doing one thing while doing the other.

name: 副词
content: 大概、必须、差不多、一定、好像、几乎
title: Adverbs of estimation and certainty
explanation: These adverbs show how sure or exact the speaker is, and they go before the verb or adjective. They are 大概 (dàgài, probably, roughly), 必须 (bìxū, must), 差不多 (chàbuduō, almost, about the same), 一定 (yídìng, definitely, must), 好像 (hǎoxiàng, seems as if) and 几乎 (jīhū, almost).

name: 副词
title: Tone adverbs (of course, actually, finally)
explanation: These adverbs add the speaker's attitude to a sentence. 当然 (dāngrán) means of course, 其实 (qíshí) means actually or in fact, and 终于 (zhōngyú) means finally, after a long wait. 才 (cái) can stress that an amount is small (only) or that only this way is right, and 就 (jiù) stresses that something is exactly or definitely so.

name: 副词
title: Negative adverbs for "no need"
explanation: 不必 (búbì, need not) and 不用 (búyòng, no need to) go before a verb to say something is unnecessary: Subject + 不必/不用 + verb. They mean you don't have to do it, not that you are forbidden.

name: 介词
title: Prepositions that introduce the target (for, toward, about)
explanation: These words introduce the person or topic an action is aimed at, and the phrase goes before the verb: Subject + preposition + target + verb. They are 为 (wèi, for, on behalf of), 向 (xiàng, toward, to a person) and 关于 (guānyú, about, concerning).

name: 介词
title: 向 for direction
explanation: 向 (xiàng, toward) introduces the direction in which something moves or faces. The pattern is Subject + 向 + direction or place + verb.

name: 介词
title: Prepositions for purpose and reason
explanation: 为了 (wèile, in order to, for the sake of) introduces the goal of an action, as in 为了 + goal, main clause. 为 (wèi, for, because of) can also introduce a reason or purpose before a verb.

name: 介词
title: 把 and 被 sentences
explanation: 把 (bǎ) puts the object before the verb to show what is done to it: Subject + 把 + object + verb + result or other element. 被 (bèi) makes a passive sentence, where the receiver comes first: Receiver + 被 + doer (optional) + verb. This means something was done to it.

name: 介词
title: 根据 (according to, based on)
explanation: 根据 (gēnjù, according to, based on) introduces the evidence or basis for a statement or action. It is usually followed by a noun or phrase, then the main clause.

name: 连词
title: "Or" between words and phrases
explanation: 或 (huò, or) and 或者 (huòzhě, or) link two words or phrases as alternatives: A + 或者 + B. They are mainly used in statements, meaning either one will do.

name: 连词
content: 只有、只要、不但、而且、如果、可1、可是、然后
title: Conjunctions linking clauses
explanation: These words join two clauses and show how they relate. 只有 (zhǐyǒu, only if) and 只要 (zhǐyào, as long as) often pair with 才 (cái) and 就 (jiù), and 不但 (búdàn, not only) pairs with 而且 (érqiě, but also). 如果 (rúguǒ) means if, 可 (kě) and 可是 (kěshì) mean but, and 然后 (ránhòu) means then, afterward.

name: 助词
title: Conditional ending 的话
explanation: 的话 (de huà, if / in that case) goes at the end of a clause to mark it as a condition: "If-clause + 的话, result". It often pairs with 如果 (rúguǒ, if) at the start of the clause, but it can stand alone.

name: 结构类型
title: Appositive phrases (a noun renamed by another)
explanation: Two noun phrases sit side by side and refer to the same person or thing, with the second one explaining or naming the first. No linking word is needed, so read them as one thing described two ways.

name: 结构类型
title: Verb + complement phrases
explanation: A verb is followed by an extra element, called a complement, that says how the action turned out or how well it was done. A common form is Verb + 得 (de) + description, such as how well or how fast something is done.

name: 结构类型
content: 数量重叠：数词+量词+数词+量词
title: Repeated number + measure word
explanation: Repeating a number and its measure word, as in Number + measure word + Number + measure word, means one by one or each in turn, as in 一个一个 (yí gè yí gè, one by one). It usually comes before the verb and describes how the action is done.

name: 固定短语
title: The 不A不B pattern
explanation: 不 (bù, not) appears twice around two words: 不 + A + 不 + B. It means neither A nor B, and often describes something that is just right or in between, such as neither too big nor too small.

name: 固定短语
title: 不一会儿 (before long)
explanation: 不一会儿 (bù yíhuìr, before long, a moment later) says that a short time passed before something happened. It usually comes before the verb or at the start of a clause.

name: 固定短语
title: 看来 (it seems)
explanation: 看来 (kànlái, it seems, it looks like) introduces a conclusion the speaker draws from what they see or know. It usually comes at the start of a sentence, followed by the conclusion.

name: 固定短语
title: 在……看来 (in someone's view)
explanation: The pattern 在 (zài) + person + 看来 (kànlái) means in someone's view or as far as someone is concerned. Put the person or group between 在 and 看来, then state the opinion.

name: 固定短语
title: 越来越 (more and more)
explanation: 越来越 (yuè lái yuè, more and more) shows a quality or feeling increasing over time. The pattern is Subject + 越来越 + adjective or feeling verb.

name: 固定短语
title: 看起来 (looks, seems)
explanation: 看起来 (kàn qǐlái, looks like, seems) gives an impression based on appearance. The pattern is Subject + 看起来 + description, or it can start a sentence.

name: 固定短语
title: 看上去 (looks, seems)
explanation: 看上去 (kàn shàngqù, looks like, seems) gives an impression based on appearance and means almost the same as 看起来 (kàn qǐlái). The pattern is Subject + 看上去 + description.

name: 固定短语
title: Set phrase 一般来说
explanation: 一般来说 (yìbān lái shuō, generally speaking) is a fixed phrase that usually opens a sentence. It introduces a general rule or the usual situation, so exceptions are possible.

name: 固定短语
title: Set phrase 不怎么样
explanation: 不怎么样 (bù zěnmeyàng, not very good, nothing special) is a fixed phrase that gives a mild negative opinion. It usually comes after the thing being judged, as a casual way to say it is just so-so or poor.

title: Besides / except with 除了
explanation: Pattern: 除了 (chúle, besides, except for) + thing A + 以外 (yǐwài, outside of; optional), then subject + 还 (hái, also) / 也 (yě, also) / 都 (dōu, all) + the rest. With 还 or 也 it means 'besides A, there is also B'; with 都 it means 'everyone or everything except A'.

title: Starting from a time or place
explanation: Pattern: 从 (cóng, from) + time or place + 起 (qǐ, starting). It marks the point where something begins and continues onward, like 'starting from...'.

title: For someone, as far as they are concerned
explanation: Pattern: 对 (duì, to, for) + person or group + 来说 (lái shuō, speaking of). It gives the point of view from which the rest of the sentence is true, like 'for X' or 'as far as X is concerned'.

title: Not even one (total negation)
explanation: Pattern: 一 (yī, one; its tone changes before other syllables) + measure word (+ noun) + 也 (yě, even) / 都 (dōu, even) + 不 (bù, not) / 没 (méi, did not, have not) + verb. It means 'not even one', a strong way to say none or not at all.

title: Not at all with 一点儿也不
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 一点儿 (yìdiǎnr, a little) + 也 (yě, even) + 不 (bù, not) + adjective or verb. It means 'not even a little', that is, 'not at all', and makes the negative very strong.

title: The more... the more... with 越
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 越 (yuè, more) + verb or adjective + 越 + verb or adjective. It says that as the first thing increases, the second increases too. The two parts can also be in separate clauses with different subjects.

title: Before and after a time or event
explanation: Pattern: (在 (zài, at, in)) + time or event + 以前 (yǐqián, before) / 以后 (yǐhòu, after), or the shorter 前 (qián, before) / 后 (hòu, after). It places something earlier or later than the stated time or event, and 在 can be left out.

title: Rhetorical 'What is there to...?' with 什么
explanation: Pattern: verb or adjective + 什么 (shénme, what) (+ 啊 (a, a softening or emphasis particle)). It is not a real question: it shows the speaker finds it unnecessary or disagrees, like 'What's there to X about?' or 'Why bother with X?'

title: Time or turn to do something with 该……了
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 该 (gāi, should, ought to) + verb + 了 (le, a particle marking a new situation). It says that now is the time or it is someone's turn to do something, or that something should be done by now.

title: Framing a situation with 在……上/下/中
explanation: Pattern: 在 (zài, at, in) + noun or phrase + 上 (shàng, on, above) / 下 (xià, under, below) / 中 (zhōng, in, within). The frame sets the area, condition or range for the rest of the sentence: 上 means 'in the matter of', 下 means 'under (certain conditions)', and 中 means 'in the midst of'.

name: 主语
content: 动词或动词性短语、形容词或形容词性短语作主语
title: Verbs and adjectives as the subject
explanation: Usually the subject is a noun, but a verb, an adjective, or a phrase built around one can come first as the thing being talked about. Pattern: verb or adjective phrase + comment about it. Read it like an English '-ing' phrase or an abstract quality.

name: 主语
title: A whole clause as the subject
explanation: A complete mini-sentence (a subject plus what it does or is) can act as the subject of a larger sentence. Pattern: [subject + verb phrase] + comment. In English this is like 'That he came...' or 'Her singing...' followed by a statement about it.

name: 定语
title: Several describing words before a noun
explanation: Chinese puts all the words that describe a noun in front of it, and 的 (de, a particle linking a describing phrase to its noun) often joins them. A common order is: owner or time/place + 的 + number + measure word + descriptive words + noun.

name: 补语
title: Result after a verb: 到, 住, 走, 上
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb + 到 (dào, reach, arrive) / 住 (zhù, hold firmly, stop) / 走 (zǒu, away) / 上 (shàng, onto, up) (+ object). The extra word after the verb tells the outcome: 到 means the goal or place was reached, 住 means it was fixed or held in place, 走 means it moved away, and 上 means it attached, closed or reached something.

name: 补语
content: 趋向补语的引申用法：（1）表示结果意义：动词+出/起/下
title: Abstract result with 出, 起, 下
explanation: Pattern: verb + 出 (chū, out) / 起 (qǐ, up) / 下 (xià, down). These direction words are used figuratively to show a result: 出 means something comes out or is identified or produced, 起 means something is raised or brought to mind, and 下 means something is settled, recorded or left in place.

name: 补语
content: （2）表示动作行为的开始：动词+上/起来
title: Starting an action with 上 or 起来
explanation: Pattern: verb + 上 (shàng, up) / 起来 (qǐlái, start up). It shows that an action or state begins, often with the sense of going on from there. With 起来, an object can come between the two syllables: verb + 起 + object + 来.

name: 补语
content: （3）表示动作行为的持续：动词+下去/下来
title: Continuing an action with 下去 or 下来
explanation: Pattern: verb + 下去 (xiàqù, go on down) / 下来 (xiàlái, come down). 下去 means an action keeps going from now into the future. 下来 means it has lasted from the past up to now, or that something has settled down or been fixed in place.

name: 补语
title: Can or cannot, with 得 and 不 after a verb
explanation: Pattern: verb + 得 (de, able to) + result or direction word means 'can'; verb + 不 (bù, not) + the same word means 'cannot'. The little word 得 or 不 sits between the verb and its result, saying whether that result is achievable.

name: 补语
title: Extremely, with 得很 after an adjective
explanation: Pattern: adjective + 得 (de, a linking particle) + 很 (hěn, very). Placed after the adjective, usually at the end of the sentence, it means 'extremely' or 'very much so'.

name: 补语
title: Extremely, with 极了 or 坏了
explanation: Pattern: adjective or verb + 极了 (jíle, extremely) / 坏了 (huàile, literally 'broken', here meaning 'terribly, to death'). It goes at the end of the phrase to show a very high degree, as in feeling something to an extreme.

name: 补语
content: 表示动作结束到某个时间点的间隔时间
title: Time since an action ended
explanation: Pattern: subject + verb + length of time + 了 (le, a particle marking a new situation). With verbs for one-off events like leaving or graduating, the time length tells how long it has been since the action ended, not how long it lasted.

name: 句类
title: Asking how with 怎样
explanation: Pattern: subject + 怎样 (zěnyàng, how) + verb. It is a question-word question asking in what way or manner something is done. The answer gives information rather than yes or no.

name: 句类
content: 用反问句表示强调：不是……吗？
title: Rhetorical question with 不是……吗
explanation: Pattern: subject + 不是 (bú shì, is not) + statement + 吗 (ma, a question particle). It is not a real question: the speaker treats the answer as obvious, so it emphasizes or reminds, like 'Isn't it...?' and means the statement is true.

name: 特殊句型
title: The 把 construction: moving something to a place
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, a word that puts the object before the verb) + object + verb + 在 (zài, at/in) or 到 (dào, to) + place. It says what someone does to a thing and where the thing ends up.

name: 特殊句型
title: The 把 construction: handing something to someone
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, a word that puts the object before the verb) + object 1 + verb (+ 给 (gěi, to give)) + object 2. Object 1 is the thing being passed, and object 2 is the person who receives it.

name: 特殊句型
content: （3）主语+把+宾语+动词+结果补语/趋向补语/状态补语
title: The 把 construction with a complement
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, a word that puts the object before the verb) + object + verb + complement. The complement is an extra word after the verb that gives the result, the direction of movement, or how or to what degree the action went.

name: 特殊句型
title: Passive sentences with 被 and a named doer
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 被 (bèi, by) + doer + verb + other element. The subject receives the action and the doer comes right after 被. The verb is not bare: something like a complement or the completed-action marker 了 (le) follows it.

name: 特殊句型
title: Passive sentences with 被 and no named doer
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 被 (bèi, by) + verb + other element. It works like the passive with a doer, but the doer is left out because it is unknown or unimportant. The subject is still the one the action happens to.

name: 特殊句型
content: “着”表示动作的伴随：动词1+着+动词2
title: Verb + 着 for an accompanying action
explanation: Pattern: Verb 1 + 着 (zhe, a marker of a continuing state) + verb 2. The first verb describes the manner or state in which the second action is done, like "doing X while Y".

name: 特殊句型
title: Comparing with 比 plus 更 or 还
explanation: Pattern: A + 比 (bǐ, compared with) + B + 更 (gèng, even more) or 还 (hái, still more) + adjective. It says A has the quality to an even greater degree than B, who already has it.

name: 特殊句型
title: Saying two things are the same with 跟……一样
explanation: Pattern: A + 跟 (gēn, with) + B + 一样 (yíyàng, the same). It says A and B are alike or identical.

name: 特殊句型
title: Equal degree with 跟……一样 plus an adjective
explanation: Pattern: A + 跟 (gēn, with) + B + 一样 (yíyàng, the same) + adjective. It says A and B are equal in that quality, such as size or speed.

name: 特殊句型
title: Negative comparison with 不比
explanation: Pattern: A + 不比 (bù bǐ, not more than) + B + adjective. It says A is not more of the quality than B, which usually means A is about equal to B or less. It is often used to correct an assumption.

name: 特殊句型
title: Comparing amounts or timing with 比
explanation: Pattern: A + 比 (bǐ, compared with) + B + 多 (duō, more) / 少 (shǎo, less) / 早 (zǎo, earlier) / 晚 (wǎn, later) + verb + quantity phrase. The quantity phrase (a number plus a measure word) says exactly how big the difference is.

name: 特殊句型
content: （1）表示出现：处所词+动词+趋向补语/结果补语+动态助词（了）+数量短语+人/物
title: Sentences describing something appearing
explanation: Pattern: Place word + verb + direction or result complement + 了 (le, marker of a completed action) + quantity phrase + person/thing. It starts with a location and tells you that someone or something has appeared there.

name: 特殊句型
content: （2）表示消失：处所词+动词+结果补语+动态助词（了）+数量短语+人/物
title: Sentences describing something disappearing
explanation: Pattern: Place word + verb + result complement + 了 (le, marker of a completed action) + quantity phrase + person/thing. It starts with a location and tells you that someone or something has gone or been lost from there.

name: 特殊句型
content: 强调说话人的看法或态度
title: 是……的 to show the speaker's opinion
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 是 (shì, is) + statement + 的 (de, a sentence-ending particle). The frame around the statement gives a firm, confident tone, showing the speaker's view or attitude rather than just reporting an event.

name: 特殊句型
content: 主语+动词+宾语+动词+补语
title: Repeating the verb before a complement
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb + object + verb + complement. The verb appears twice: first with its object, then again followed by a complement that says how well, how long, or to what degree the action goes. A linking word like 得 (de) often comes before that complement.

name: 复句
title: Sequence with 先……，再/然后……
explanation: Pattern: 先 (xiān, first) + first action, 再 (zài, then) or 然后 (ránhòu, after that) + next action. It lists actions in the order they happen.

name: 复句
title: Alternatives with 或者……，或者……
explanation: Pattern: 或者 (huòzhě, or) + option 1, 或者 + option 2. It offers choices in a statement, meaning "either this or that".

name: 复句
title: Alternating states with 一会儿……，一会儿……
explanation: Pattern: 一会儿 (yíhuìr, for a little while) + situation 1, 一会儿 + situation 2. It describes things switching back and forth, like "one moment this, the next moment that".

name: 复句
title: Two qualities at once with 又……，又……
explanation: Pattern: 又 (yòu, also) + quality or action 1, 又 + quality or action 2. It means "both ... and ...", joining two things true of the same subject.

name: 复句
title: Simultaneous actions with 一边……，一边……
explanation: Pattern: 一边 (yìbiān, at the same time) + action 1, 一边 + action 2. The same person does two actions at the same time, like "while doing X, doing Y".

name: 复句
title: Adding more with 不但……，而且……
explanation: Pattern: 不但 (búdàn, not only) + statement 1, 而且 (érqiě, but also) + statement 2. The second part adds something further, usually stronger than the first.

name: 复句
title: Contrast with 虽然……，可是……
explanation: Pattern: 虽然 (suīrán, although) + statement 1, 可是 (kěshì, but) + statement 2. The first part grants a fact and the second part gives a contrasting point that goes against expectation.

name: 复句
title: If-then with 如果……，就……
explanation: Pattern: 如果 (rúguǒ, if) + condition, 就 (jiù, then) + result. The first part sets up a hypothetical situation and the second part says what follows from it.

name: 复句
title: If-then with ……的话，就……
explanation: Pattern: condition + 的话 (dehuà, if that is the case), 就 (jiù, then) + result. 的话 comes at the end of the condition part, which is the "if" clause, and 就 introduces what follows.

name: 复句
title: Only-if with 只有……，才……
explanation: Pattern: 只有 (zhǐyǒu, only if) + condition, 才 (cái, only then) + result. The condition is the one and only way to get the result, so without it the result does not happen.

name: 复句
title: Condition clauses with 只要……就……
explanation: Pattern: 只要 (zhǐyào, as long as) + condition, (Subject +) 就 (jiù, then) + result. The first part gives the one condition needed, and the second part says what follows once it is met.

name: 复句
title: Purpose clauses with 为了
explanation: Pattern: 为了 (wèile, in order to / for the sake of) + goal, main clause. The 为了 part names the aim, and the rest of the sentence says what is done to reach it.

name: 复句
title: Compressed two-step sentences with 了 and 就
explanation: Pattern: Action 1 + 了 (le, marks the action as done) + (就 jiù, then) + Action 2. Two actions are packed into one sentence with no comma, meaning that once the first is done, the second follows.

name: 数的表达法
content: 概数表达法2：（1）用“大概”表示概数
title: Approximate numbers with 大概
explanation: Pattern: 大概 (dàgài, approximately) + number + measure word + noun. Put 大概 before the number to show the amount is a rough estimate, not exact.

name: 数的表达法
title: Approximate numbers with two neighboring numbers
explanation: Pattern: Number + next number + measure word + noun. Two numbers that are next to each other in counting, such as 三 (sān, three) and 四 (sì, four), placed side by side mean about that amount, here roughly three or four.

name: 动词
title: The modal verb 敢 (to dare)
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 敢 (gǎn, dare) + verb. It says someone has the courage to do something; the negative 不敢 (bù gǎn, not dare) means someone does not dare to do it.

name: 代词
title: Words meaning each, every, any and this
explanation: 各 (gè, each/every) goes before a noun or measure word to mean every one of a group. 各位 (gèwèi, everyone, polite) addresses an audience, 各种 (gèzhǒng, all kinds of) goes before a noun, 任何 (rènhé, any) means no matter which, and 此 (cǐ, this) is a formal word for this.

name: 量词
title: Specific measure words for nouns
explanation: Pattern: Number + measure word + noun. 打 (dá, dozen), 袋 (dài, bag of), 棵 (kē, for trees and plants), 台 (tái, for machines and appliances) and 幅 (fú, for paintings and pictures) are measure words tied to particular kinds of things.

name: 量词
content: （2）借用名量词：脸、手、盒、屋子、桌子
title: Nouns borrowed as measure words
explanation: Pattern: Number + noun used as measure word + noun. 脸 (liǎn, face), 手 (shǒu, hand), 盒 (hé, box), 屋子 (wūzi, room) and 桌子 (zhuōzi, table) can serve as containers or spaces, so the phrase means a faceful, handful, boxful, roomful or tableful of something.

name: 量词
title: Measure words for actions
explanation: Pattern: Verb + number + measure word. 场 (chǎng, for events such as games, films and shows), 顿 (dùn, for meals, scoldings and beatings) and 趟 (tàng, for trips there and back) count how many times an action happens.

name: 副词
content: 十分、更加、稍、稍微、尤其、多么
title: Degree adverbs
explanation: These words go before an adjective or feeling verb to say how much. 十分 (shífēn, very), 更加 (gèngjiā, even more), 稍 (shāo, slightly), 稍微 (shāowēi, a little), 尤其 (yóuqí, especially), 多么 (duōme, how/so, often in exclamations).

name: 副词
title: Adverbs of scope or extent
explanation: These go before the verb to say how much or how many are included. 共 (gòng, altogether), 全 (quán, all/entirely), 光 (guāng, only/merely), 仅 (jǐn, only), 仅仅 (jǐnjǐn, only/merely, stronger), 至少 (zhìshǎo, at least).

name: 副词
content: 按时、从来、赶紧、赶快、已、忽然、将、将要、从、本来
title: Time adverbs
explanation: These go before the verb to say when or how an action fits in time. 按时 (ànshí, on time), 从来 (cónglái, all along, usually with a negative: never), 赶紧 (gǎnjǐn, hurriedly), 赶快 (gǎnkuài, quickly), 已 (yǐ, already, formal), 忽然 (hūrán, suddenly), 将 (jiāng, will/about to), 将要 (jiāngyào, be about to), 从 (cóng, ever, as in 从不 cóng bù, never), 本来 (běnlái, originally).

name: 副词
title: Frequency adverbs
explanation: These go before the verb to say how often something happens. 重新 (chóngxīn, anew/starting over), 往往 (wǎngwǎng, often, as a general pattern), 偶尔 (ǒu'ěr, occasionally), 再次 (zàicì, once more), 老 (lǎo, always/constantly, informal).

name: 副词
title: Adverbs of manner
explanation: These go before the verb to describe how an action is done. 故意 (gùyì, on purpose), 互相 (hùxiāng, each other/one another), 相互 (xiānghù, mutually, more formal).

name: 副词
title: The contrast adverb 却
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 却 (què, but/yet/however) + verb or adjective. It goes after the subject and shows a result that goes against what you would expect from the first part of the sentence.

name: 副词
title: Adverbs of possibility
explanation: These go before the verb to show a guess. 也许 (yěxǔ, perhaps/maybe) is a general guess, and 恐怕 (kǒngpà, I'm afraid that/probably) is a guess that usually sounds worried or regretful.

name: 副词
content: 才4、就5、并1、还4、竟然、究竟、正好、到底、难道、千万、确实、只好、差（一）点儿
title: Adverbs that add tone or emphasis
explanation: These go before the verb and add attitude. 才 (cái, only just/not until), 就 (jiù, right away/exactly), 并 (bìng, in fact, placed before a negative to stress it), 还 (hái, even/still, adding emphasis), 竟然 (jìngrán, unexpectedly), 究竟 (jiūjìng, exactly/on earth, in questions), 正好 (zhènghǎo, just right), 到底 (dàodǐ, after all/in the end), 难道 (nándào, could it be that, in rhetorical questions), 千万 (qiānwàn, be sure to), 确实 (quèshí, truly), 只好 (zhǐhǎo, have no choice but to), 差（一）点儿 (chà (yì) diǎnr, almost).

name: 介词
title: Prepositions for time and place
explanation: Pattern: Preposition + time/place/event + main clause. 自 (zì, from), 当 (dāng, at the time when), 由 (yóu, from/starting from), 随着 (suízhe, along with/as something changes), 等 (děng, when/by the time that).

name: 介词
title: Prepositions that mark who does what to what
explanation: 将 (jiāng, a formal version of 把 bǎ) is used as Subject + 将 + receiver + verb. 叫 (jiào, by) and 让 (ràng, by) mark the doer in passive sentences: Receiver + 叫/让 + doer + verb. 由 (yóu, by) names the person responsible: 由 + doer + verb.

name: 介词
title: The reason preposition 由于
explanation: Pattern: 由于 (yóuyú, because of/due to) + reason, result. It introduces the cause and is more formal than 因为 (yīnwèi, because).

name: 介词
title: Prepositions that introduce the target
explanation: 对于 (duìyú, regarding/as for) introduces the topic being discussed: 对于 + topic, comment. 与 (yǔ, with) introduces the other party: Subject + 与 + person + verb.

name: 介词
title: Prepositions for role, basis or standard
explanation: Pattern: Preposition + role or standard + verb. 作为 (zuòwéi, as/in the role of) gives a role. 按 (àn, according to) and 按照 (ànzhào, in accordance with) give a rule or standard that is followed.

name: 连词
title: Conjunctions joining words or phrases
explanation: These link two words or phrases of the same kind. 并 (bìng, and also, linking verbs), 而 (ér, and/yet, linking adjectives or contrasting ideas), 与 (yǔ, and, linking nouns).

name: 连词
content: 此外、而2、既然、甚至、不过、并且
title: Conjunctions linking clauses or sentences
explanation: These connect one clause or sentence to the next. 此外 (cǐwài, besides this), 而 (ér, but/whereas), 既然 (jìrán, since/now that), 甚至 (shènzhì, even), 不过 (búguò, however), 并且 (bìngqiě, and also).

name: 连词
content: 不光、不仅、另外、要是、因此、由于2、加
title: Conjunctions linking clauses
explanation: These words connect two clauses or sentences. 不光 (bùguāng, not only) and 不仅 (bùjǐn, not only) introduce the first half of an 'and also' idea. 另外 (lìngwài, in addition) adds a further point, 要是 (yàoshi, if) sets a condition, and 因此 (yīncǐ, therefore) introduces a result. 由于 (yóuyú, because/due to) introduces a reason, and 加 (jiā, plus, on top of that) adds one more thing.

name: 助词
title: Other particles: 等, 者, 之, 就是
explanation: 等 (děng, and so on) ends a list and shows there are more items. 者 (zhě, one who) attaches to a word to mean 'a person who does or is that'. 之 (zhī, a formal word for 'of') links two parts, and 就是 (jiùshì, that's all) can close a statement to show something is simple or certain.

name: 叹词
title: Interjections 啊 and 嗯
explanation: These are sound words that show a reaction rather than add meaning. 啊 (a, ah) expresses surprise, realization, or emphasis. 嗯 (èn, mm/uh-huh) shows agreement, acknowledgment, or thinking. They usually stand apart from the rest of the sentence.

name: 结构类型
title: Number + adjective + measure word
explanation: An adjective can sit between a number and a measure word (a counting word) to describe the size or amount of the thing counted. Pattern: Number + adjective + measure word + (noun). Read the adjective as describing the noun that follows.

name: 固定短语
title: The four-character pattern 一A一B
explanation: This is a four-character phrase built on 一 (yī, one) repeated, with two words A and B filling the slots. It usually pictures two actions or things happening in turn or as a pair, like 'one A, one B'. Pattern: 一 + A + 一 + B.

name: 固定短语
title: The four-character pattern 无A无B
explanation: This four-character phrase uses 无 (wú, without, no) twice to mean 'no A and no B'. A and B are usually related words, and the phrase describes someone or something lacking both. Pattern: 无 + A + 无 + B.

name: 固定短语
title: The four-character pattern 有A有B
explanation: This four-character phrase uses 有 (yǒu, to have) twice to mean 'having both A and B'. A and B are usually related words, and the phrase often paints a full or lively picture. Pattern: 有 + A + 有 + B.

name: 固定短语
title: 来得及 and 来不及: have time / no time
explanation: 来得及 (láidejí) means there is still enough time to do something, and 来不及 (láibují) means there is not enough time, so it is too late. Pattern: Subject + 来得及/来不及 + verb.

name: 固定短语
title: 有的是: plenty of
explanation: 有的是 (yǒudeshì) means 'there is plenty of' or 'have lots of', and it stresses that supply is abundant. Pattern: Subject + 有的是 + noun. Don't confuse it with 有的 (yǒude, some).

name: 固定短语
title: 说不定: maybe
explanation: 说不定 (shuōbudìng) means 'perhaps' or 'it could be that', and it shows you cannot be sure. It usually comes before a verb or a whole clause to mark a possibility.

name: 固定短语
title: 不怎么: not very
explanation: 不怎么 combines 不 (bù, not) and 怎么 (zěnme, how) to mean 'not very' or 'not particularly'. It softens a negative statement. Pattern: Subject + 不怎么 + adjective/verb.

name: 固定短语
title: 就是说 and 这就是说: in other words
explanation: 就是说 (jiùshì shuō, that is to say) and 这就是说 (zhè jiùshì shuō, this means) introduce a restatement, explanation, or conclusion of what was just said. Read what follows as 'in other words…'.

title: Steady change: 一 + measure word + 比 + 一 + measure word
explanation: This pattern shows something changing step by step, as in 'each one more … than the one before'. It repeats the same measure word on both sides of 比 (bǐ, compared with), with 一 (yī, one) in front of each. Pattern: 一 + measure word + 比 + 一 + same measure word + adjective/verb.

title: 在……方面: in the area of
explanation: This frame marks the topic or aspect being talked about, meaning 'in terms of' or 'regarding'. 在 (zài, at, in) comes first and 方面 (fāngmiàn, aspect, area) comes last, with the topic between them. Pattern: 在 + topic + 方面 + comment.

title: 够……的: quite, really
explanation: This pattern stresses that something reaches a high degree, often with a feeling of complaint or surprise. 够 (gòu, enough) comes before an adjective or verb and 的 (de) ends the phrase. Pattern: Subject + 够 + adjective/verb + 的.

title: 拿……来说: take … as an example
explanation: This frame picks one thing as an example or a starting point for a comment, like 'speaking of' or 'take … for instance'. 拿 (ná, take) comes before the item and 来说 (láishuō, to speak of) follows it. Pattern: 拿 + thing + 来说, + comment.

title: 再也不/没……: never again
explanation: 再也 (zài yě, never again, no longer) is followed by 不 (bù, not) or 没 (méi, did not) to say something will not, or did not, happen any more. Pattern: Subject + 再也 + 不/没 + verb. 不 is about a decision or habit, while 没 is about something that has not happened since.

title: 怎么都/也不/没……: no matter how
explanation: This pattern means 'no matter how one tries, it still doesn't work out'. 怎么 (zěnme, how) comes first, then 都 (dōu, all) or 也 (yě, also, even), then 不 (bù, not) or 没 (méi, did not) with the verb. Pattern: Subject + 怎么 + verb + 都/也 + 不/没 + result.

title: 为了……而……: doing something for a goal
explanation: This frame says someone does an action for the sake of a goal. 为了 (wèile, in order to, for the sake of) introduces the goal and 而 (ér, a linking word) connects it to the action. Pattern: Subject + 为了 + goal + 而 + verb.

title: Verb + 一X是一X: as much as you can
explanation: This pattern repeats the same word X (often a measure word) after 一 (yī, one) and 是 (shì, is). It means 'take it one X at a time' or 'whatever little you get counts', with a sense of making do. Pattern: verb + 一 + X + 是 + 一 + X.

title: （没）有什么（好）X的: nothing worth X-ing
explanation: This frame says there is nothing worth doing or nothing to be bothered by. It uses 有 (yǒu, have), optionally 没 (méi, not), plus 什么 (shénme, what), optionally 好 (hǎo, good, worth), then a verb X and 的 (de). Without 没 it is a rhetorical question, as in 'what is there to X?'. Pattern: (没)有什么(好) + verb + 的.

title: X是X，Y是Y: keeping things separate
explanation: Repeating a word on both sides of 是 (shì, is) says that each thing is what it is and should be kept distinct from the other. Pattern: X + 是 + X, Y + 是 + Y. It is used to separate two things or two matters that should not be mixed up.

title: X也得X，不X也得X: must either way
explanation: This pattern means you have to do X whether you want to or not. 也 (yě, also, even) and 得 (děi, must) appear in both halves, and 不 (bù, not) negates X in the second half. Pattern: X + 也 + 得 + X, 不 + X + 也 + 得 + X. X is usually a verb.

title: X就是了: that's all there is to it
explanation: Ending a clause with 就是了 (jiù shì le, that's all, and that's it) reassures the listener that something is simple or nothing to worry about. Pattern: Clause + 就是了. Think of it as 'just do X and it's fine'.

title: 还X呢: ironic 'and you call that X?'
explanation: This pattern is sarcastic and points out that what someone says or claims does not match reality. 还 (hái, still, yet) comes before X and the particle 呢 (ne) ends the phrase. Pattern: Subject + 还 + X + 呢. Read it as 'and you're supposed to be X?'.

title: Telling someone to carry on with their own business
