explanation: Pattern: 你 (nǐ, you) + verb + 你的 (nǐ de, your own) + 吧 (ba, a softening particle). The same verb is repeated, and the speaker is saying 'you go ahead and do your thing', often meaning 'don't worry about me'.

title: Just do what you're told
explanation: Pattern: 让/叫 (ràng/jiào, tell or order) + 你 (nǐ, you) + verb + 你 (nǐ, you) + 就 (jiù, then just) + the same verb. It means 'when you are told to do X, just do X', with no arguing.

title: Must do it no matter what
explanation: Pattern: 说什么/怎么 (shuō shénme / zěnme, say what / how) + optional 着 (zhe, a particle that can be left out) + 也 (yě, still) + 得 (děi, must) + verb. It expresses 'no matter what, one has to do X', a firm insistence.

title: Resigned acceptance: 'then just X, I suppose'
explanation: Pattern: word X + 就 (jiù, then) + the same word X + optional 点儿 (diǎnr, a bit) + 吧 (ba, a softening particle). The speaker accepts a situation or a small compromise, as in 'if it is X, then let it be X'.

title: Granting a point, then adding 'but'
explanation: Pattern: word X + 是 (shì, to be) + the same word X, usually followed by a clause of contrast. It means 'yes, it is X (but...)': the speaker admits the point, then adds a limit or objection.

content: 形容词/心理动词+死了/厉害
title: Extreme degree with 死了 or 厉害
explanation: Pattern: adjective or feeling verb + 死了 (sǐ le, literally 'to death', meaning extremely) or + 厉害 (lìhai, terribly, intensely), where 厉害 is often linked with 得 (de, a linking particle). It says the quality or feeling is very strong.

title: Can or cannot, with 得了 / 不了
explanation: Pattern: verb + 得 (de, can) / 不 (bù, cannot) + 了 (liǎo, to finish or manage). It says whether something is possible, as in being able or unable to finish, handle, or bear it; here 了 is read liǎo, not le.

name: 句类
title: 'Could it be that...?' rhetorical questions
explanation: Pattern: 难道 (nándào, could it be that / surely not) + statement + 吗 (ma, question particle). It is not a real request for information; it shows surprise or doubt and suggests the speaker expects the opposite.

name: 句类
content: 由疑问代词构成的反问句
title: Rhetorical questions with question words
explanation: A question word such as 谁 (shéi, who), 什么 (shénme, what), 怎么 (zěnme, how), 哪儿 (nǎr, where) or 为什么 (wèishénme, why) is used to make a point rather than ask for information. The meaning usually flips: the question implies a strong statement of the opposite.

name: 特殊句型
title: The 把 construction with a repeated verb
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, takes the object and does something to it) + object + verb + optional 一 (yi, one) or 了 (le, completed) + the same verb. The repeated verb makes the action short, casual or a quick try, and it is done to the object.

name: 特殊句型
title: The 把 construction with 了
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, takes the object and does something to it) + object + verb + 了 (le, marks completion). It says the subject dealt with the object and the action is done.

name: 特殊句型
content: （3）主语+把+宾语+动词+动量补语/时量补语
title: The 把 construction with a number of times or a length of time
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, takes the object and does something to it) + object + verb + how many times / how long. The words after the verb tell how many times the action happened or how long it lasted.

name: 特殊句型
title: The 把 construction with an adverbial before the verb
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, takes the object and does something to it) + object + adverbial + verb. The adverbial is a word or phrase before the verb that says how, when or where the action is done to the object.

name: 特殊句型
content: 主语+叫/让+宾语+动词+其他成分
title: Passive sentences with 叫 or 让
explanation: Pattern: Subject (the receiver) + 叫/让 (jiào/ràng, by) + doer + verb + another element such as a result or 了 (le, completed). The subject is the one acted upon, and the person doing it comes after 叫 or 让; this is the casual, spoken way to say 'by'.

name: 特殊句型
content: （1）表爱憎义：主语+表扬/批评+宾语1+动词+宾语2
title: Praising or criticizing someone for what they did
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 表扬/批评 (biǎoyáng/pīpíng, praise/criticize) + person + verb + object. The person after the first verb is also the one doing the second verb, so the sentence says who is praised or blamed and for what.

name: 特殊句型
content: （2）表称谓或认定义：主语+收/选+宾语1+做/当/为+宾语2
title: Taking or choosing someone as a role
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 收/选 (shōu/xuǎn, take in/choose) + person + 做/当/为 (zuò/dāng/wéi, as / to be) + role. It says someone is taken, chosen or named as a certain role or title.

name: 特殊句型
content: （3）表致使：主语+使/让+人称代词+动词短语
title: Making someone feel or do something
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 使/让 (shǐ/ràng, make or cause) + pronoun + verb phrase. The subject is a cause that makes a person feel or do something.

title: Comparing with 不如: 'not as good as'
explanation: Pattern: A + 不如 (bùrú, not as good as) + B + optional adjective. It says A does not measure up to B, either in the quality named by the adjective or in general.

title: Comparing with 跟……相比
explanation: Pattern: 跟 (gēn, with) + A + 相比 (xiāngbǐ, compare), then a statement about B. It means 'compared with A, ...' and sets up the comparison before the main point.

title: Double negatives for emphasis
explanation: Two negative words in the same sentence cancel each other out and make a strong positive meaning, such as 不得不 (bù dé bù, have no choice but to) or 非……不可 (fēi...bùkě, must). Look for two negatives like 不 (bù, not) or 没 (méi, not have) close together.

name: 复句
title: 'Not A, but rather B'
explanation: Pattern: 不是 (bú shì, is not) + A, 而是 (ér shì, but rather) + B. It rejects the first option and states the correct one.

name: 复句
title: 'Both A and B'
explanation: Pattern: 既 (jì, both) + A, 又/也 (yòu/yě, and also) + B. It joins two qualities or actions of the same subject.

name: 复句
title: 'On one hand... on the other hand...'
explanation: Pattern: 一方面 (yì fāngmiàn, on one hand) + point 1, 另一方面 (lìng yì fāngmiàn, on the other hand) + point 2. It presents two aspects of a situation or two reasons side by side.

name: 复句
title: 'First of all... second...'
explanation: Pattern: 首先 (shǒuxiān, first of all) + point 1, 其次 (qícì, second, next) + point 2. It lists points or steps in order of importance or sequence.

name: 复句
title: 'First... then...'
explanation: Pattern: 首先 (shǒuxiān, first of all) + step 1, 然后 (ránhòu, then, afterwards) + step 2. It describes actions in the order they happen.

name: 复句
title: Sequence of events with 于是
explanation: 于是 (yúshì, so / then) begins a second clause describing what happened or was done as a result of, or right after, the first. Pattern: Clause 1, + 于是 + Clause 2.

name: 复句
title: Escalation with 甚至
explanation: 甚至 (shènzhì, even / to the point that) introduces a more extreme case that goes beyond the first statement. Pattern: Clause 1, + 甚至 + more extreme thing.

name: 复句
title: Not only... but also...
explanation: 不仅 (bùjǐn, not only) or 不光 (bùguāng, not only) opens the first part, and 还 (hái, also) or 而且 (érqiě, moreover) adds something further in the second. Pattern: 不仅/不光 + Clause 1, + 还/而且 + Clause 2.

name: 复句
title: Adding more with 并且
explanation: 并且 (bìngqiě, and also / moreover) links a second action, quality or clause that adds to the first. Pattern: Clause 1, + 并且 + added information.

name: 复句
title: Even... let alone... with 连 and 更
explanation: 连 (lián, even) marks an extreme example, followed by 也 (yě, also) or 都 (dōu, even) and a verb. The next clause then uses 更 (gèng, even more) to say the other case is even more so. Pattern: 连 + extreme example + 也/都 + verb, ... + 更 + ...

name: 复句
title: Either... or... with 不是……就是……
explanation: 不是 (bú shì, is not) followed by 就是 (jiù shì, then it is) says that if it is not the first thing, it is the second, with no third option. It often describes a repeated pattern. Pattern: 不是 + A, + 就是 + B.

name: 复句
title: Although... but... with 尽管
explanation: 尽管 (jǐnguǎn, although / even though) opens a fact that is admitted, and 但是 (dànshì, but) or 可是 (kěshì, but) introduces the contrasting result. Pattern: 尽管 + Clause 1, + 但是/可是 + Clause 2.

name: 复句
title: Contrast with 然而
explanation: 然而 (rán'ér, however / yet) is a fairly formal word for "but" that starts a clause contradicting or contrasting with the previous one. Pattern: Clause 1, + 然而 + contrasting clause.

name: 复句
title: Softer contrast with 不过
explanation: 不过 (búguò, but / however) adds a limit, drawback or mild contrast to what was just said, softer than 但是 (dànshì, but). Pattern: Clause 1, + 不过 + qualifying clause.

name: 复句
title: Granting a point with X是X
explanation: A word is repeated around 是 (shì, is) to concede that it is true, and 就是 (jiùshì, it's just that) or 不过 (búguò, but) then brings in a drawback. Pattern: X + 是 + X, + 就是/不过 + drawback.

name: 复句
title: Otherwise with 否则
explanation: 否则 (fǒuzé, otherwise / or else) starts a clause saying what would happen if the first clause were not true or not done. Pattern: Clause 1, + 否则 + unwelcome consequence.

name: 复句
title: If... then... with 要是
explanation: 要是 (yàoshi, if) sets up a supposed situation, and 就 (jiù, then) introduces the result. Pattern: 要是 + Condition, + Subject + 就 + Result.

name: 复句
title: If... then... otherwise...
explanation: This extends 要是 (yàoshi, if) with an optional 就 (jiù, then) for the result and 否则 (fǒuzé, otherwise) for what happens if the condition is not met. Pattern: 要是 + Condition, + (就) + Result, + 否则 + Alternative result.

name: 复句
title: No matter... with 不管
explanation: 不管 (bùguǎn, no matter) is followed by a question word or a list of alternatives, and the second part, with 都 (dōu, all / still) or 也 (yě, also / still), says the result stays the same. Pattern: 不管 + options, + Subject + 都/也 + Result.

name: 复句
title: Regardless of... with 无论
explanation: 无论 (wúlùn, regardless of / no matter) works like 不管 (bùguǎn, no matter) but is more formal. The second part uses 都 (dōu, all / still) or 也 (yě, also / still) to say the result is unchanged. Pattern: 无论 + options, + Subject + 都/也 + Result.

name: 复句
title: Since... then... with 既然
explanation: 既然 (jìrán, since / now that) states a fact already known or accepted, and 就 (jiù, then) gives the natural conclusion, suggestion or question that follows from it. Pattern: 既然 + Known fact, + Subject + 就 + Conclusion.

name: 复句
title: Because... therefore... with 由于 and 因此
explanation: 由于 (yóuyú, because / due to) gives the reason and can be left out, while 因此 (yīncǐ, therefore) introduces the result. This is a fairly formal pair. Pattern: (由于) + Reason, + 因此 + Result.

name: 复句
title: So that... with 好
explanation: 好 (hǎo) at the start of a second clause means "so that" or "in order to make it easy to". It gives the purpose of the first clause. Pattern: Clause 1 (an action), + 好 + easier purpose.

name: 复句
title: Even if... with 即使
explanation: 即使 (jíshǐ, even if) raises a possible or extreme situation, and 也 (yě, still) in the second part says the result does not change. Pattern: 即使 + Situation, + Subject + 也 + Result.

name: 复句
title: Even if... with 就是
explanation: 就是 (jiùshì, even if) is a more casual way to say "even if", paired with 也 (yě, still) in the second part to show the result stays the same. Pattern: 就是 + Situation, + Subject + 也 + Result.

name: 复句
title: Compressed sentences with no linking word
explanation: Two short parts are run together without a pause or a connecting word like "if" or "because". You work out from the meaning whether the link is sequence, condition or cause, and the second part usually follows from the first.

name: 复句
title: Even without... with 不……也……
explanation: A negative verb phrase with 不 (bù, not) is followed directly by 也 (yě, also / still) and a second phrase, meaning "even if not X, still Y". The two parts are squeezed into one short sentence. Pattern: 不 + X + 也 + Y.

name: 数的表示法
content: 概数表示法3：数词+来+量词
title: Approximate numbers with 来
explanation: 来 (lái, about / or so) placed right after a number gives a rough amount, often a round number like ten. Pattern: Number + 来 + measure word + noun.

name: 数的表示法
content: 用“大约、左右、前后”表示概数
title: Approximate numbers with 大约, 左右 and 前后
explanation: 大约 (dàyuē, approximately) goes before a number or amount, while 左右 (zuǒyòu, around / or so) goes after it. 前后 (qiánhòu, around / about) goes after a time or date to mean shortly before or after it. Patterns: 大约 + Number + measure word; Number + measure word + 左右; Time + 前后.

name: 数的表示法
content: 小数、分数、百分数、倍数的表示法
title: Decimals, fractions, percentages and multiples
explanation: Decimals use 点 (diǎn, point) between the whole number and the digits after it. Fractions are said denominator first: bottom number + 分之 (fēn zhī, parts of) + top number. Percentages use 百分之 (bǎi fēn zhī, percent) + number, and multiples use 倍 (bèi, times / -fold) after a number.

name: 后缀
title: Noun suffix 头
explanation: A suffix is a piece added to the end of a word. 头 (tou, normally tóu, head) is added after a root to form a noun, and in this use it is unstressed and no longer means 'head'. Pattern: Root + 头.

name: 代词
title: Demonstrative pronouns 彼此, 如此, 本
explanation: These are words that point to things. 彼此 (bǐcǐ, each other, both sides) refers to two parties. 如此 (rúcǐ, like this, so) replaces a described manner or degree. 本 (běn, this, the present, our own) goes before a noun in a formal style: 本 + noun.

name: 量词
content: 册、朵、届、颗、匹、行、架、群、支、根、批、束、副、集、周
title: Measure words for nouns (册, 朵, 届, 颗, etc.)
explanation: A measure word sits between a number or 这/那 and a noun: Number + measure word + noun. Here: 册 (cè, copies of a book), 朵 (duǒ, flowers, clouds), 届 (jiè, sessions of a recurring event or graduating classes), 颗 (kē, small round things), 匹 (pǐ, horses), 行 (háng, rows or lines), 架 (jià, planes, pianos and other framed machines), 群 (qún, groups, crowds), 支 (zhī, pens, sticks, teams, songs), 根 (gēn, long thin things), 批 (pī, batches), 束 (shù, bundles, bouquets), 副 (fù, pairs or sets), 集 (jí, episodes or volumes), 周 (zhōu, weeks).

name: 量词
title: Measure word for actions: 眼
explanation: 眼 (yǎn, a glance, literally 'eye') counts how many looks someone gives. It follows a looking verb and a number: Verb + number + 眼.

name: 副词
content: 过于、相当、较1、可2、格外、极其
title: Degree adverbs
explanation: These words go before an adjective or verb to say how strong it is: 过于 (guòyú, excessively), 相当 (xiāngdāng, fairly, quite), 较 (jiào, comparatively), 可 (kě, really, very, as spoken emphasis), 格外 (géwài, especially), 极其 (jíqí, extremely). Pattern: Subject + degree adverb + adjective/verb.

name: 副词
content: 时刻、曾经、立刻、连忙、始终、早已、即将、急忙、渐渐、尽快、早晚
title: Time adverbs
explanation: These words go before the verb to say when or how long something happens: 时刻 (shíkè, at every moment), 曾经 (céngjīng, once, previously), 立刻 (lìkè, immediately), 连忙 (liánmáng, promptly), 始终 (shǐzhōng, all along), 早已 (zǎoyǐ, long since), 即将 (jíjiāng, about to), 急忙 (jímáng, hurriedly), 渐渐 (jiànjiàn, gradually), 尽快 (jǐnkuài, as soon as possible), 早晚 (zǎowǎn, sooner or later).

name: 副词
title: Frequency adverbs
explanation: These words go before a verb to say how often something happens: 老是 (lǎoshi, always, often with a complaint), 通常 (tōngcháng, usually), 时常 (shícháng, often).

name: 副词
title: Adverbs of manner
explanation: These words go before a verb to say how an action is done: 尽量 (jǐnliàng, as much as possible) and 亲自 (qīnzì, personally, in person).

name: 副词
title: Linking adverbs 便 and 一旦
explanation: These adverbs tie two clauses together. 一旦 (yídàn, once, if ever) opens a condition, and 便 (biàn, then, right away; a formal version of 就) introduces the result. Pattern: 一旦 + condition, (subject) + 便 + result.

name: 副词
title: Adverbs of appearance: 似乎 and 仿佛
explanation: 似乎 (sìhū, it seems, seemingly) and 仿佛 (fǎngfú, as if, seemingly) go before a verb or clause to say how things appear rather than state them as fact.

name: 副词
content: 毕竟、居然、反正、根本、果然、简直、绝对、的确、反而、白、刚好、可3
title: Adverbs of tone and attitude
explanation: These words show the speaker's attitude toward what is said: 毕竟 (bìjìng, after all), 居然 (jūrán, unexpectedly), 反正 (fǎnzhèng, anyway), 根本 (gēnběn, at all, usually with a negative), 果然 (guǒrán, sure enough), 简直 (jiǎnzhí, simply, virtually), 绝对 (juéduì, absolutely), 的确 (díquè, indeed), 反而 (fǎn'ér, on the contrary, instead), 白 (bái, in vain, for nothing), 刚好 (gānghǎo, just right, happening to), 可 (kě, emphatic 'indeed, really'). They usually come before the verb or adjective.

name: 介词
title: Preposition 自从 (since)
explanation: 自从 (zìcóng, since) introduces the starting point in the past from which a situation continues or changes. Pattern: 自从 + past time or event, + clause describing what followed.

name: 介词
title: Prepositions of direction 朝 and 沿着
explanation: 朝 (cháo, toward, facing) gives the direction of an action, and 沿着 (yánzhe, along; 着 may be dropped) gives the path followed. Patterns: 朝 + direction/place + verb; 沿(着) + road/river/edge + verb.

name: 介词
title: Prepositions 替, 同 and 较
explanation: These introduce the person or thing an action involves. 替 (tì, for, on behalf of): 替 + person + verb. 同 (tóng, with, same as 跟): 同 + person + verb. 较 (jiào, than, a formal comparison): A + 较 + B + adjective.

name: 介词
title: Preposition 凭 (based on)
explanation: 凭 (píng, by relying on, based on) introduces what something depends on, such as ability or evidence. Pattern: 凭 + thing relied on + verb/clause.

name: 介词
title: Preposition 据 (according to)
explanation: 据 (jù, according to) introduces the source of information, usually in news or formal writing. Pattern: 据 + source, + statement.

name: 介词
title: Preposition 依据 (on the basis of)
explanation: 依据 (yījù, on the basis of, according to) introduces the rule, facts or evidence that a decision or judgment rests on. Pattern: 依据 + basis, + verb/clause.

name: 连词
title: Conjunctions joining words: 以及 and 同
explanation: These join two nouns or phrases. 以及 (yǐjí, as well as, and) often adds a further item to a list, and 同 (tóng, and, same as 和) joins two items. Pattern: A + 以及/同 + B.

name: 连词
title: Conjunctions joining clauses
explanation: These link one clause or sentence to the next: 从而 (cóng'ér, thus, thereby) gives a result, 可见 (kějiàn, so it is clear that) draws a conclusion, 假如 (jiǎrú, if, suppose) sets a condition, and 总之 (zǒngzhī, in short) sums up.

name: 助词
title: Particle 似的 (as if, like)
explanation: 似的 (shìde, as if, just like) goes after a noun, verb or phrase to say something resembles it. Pattern: Noun/verb phrase + 似的.

name: 固定短语
title: Repeated verb pattern A来A去
explanation: Repeat the same verb A around 来 (lái, come) and 去 (qù, go) to show an action done over and over or back and forth. Pattern: Verb + 来 + same verb + 去.

name: 固定短语
title: Repeated verb pattern A着A着
explanation: Repeat the same verb A with 着 (zhe, marks an ongoing action) after each. It means 'while doing A', and a new situation or sudden change follows. Pattern: Verb + 着 + same verb + 着, + what happened.

name: 固定短语
title: Pattern 没A没B
explanation: 没 (méi, not have) is placed before two related words, A and B, to mean 'with no A and no B'. It often criticizes a lack of proper behavior or order. Pattern: 没 + A + 没 + B.

name: 固定短语
title: Pattern 说A就A
explanation: The same verb A appears after 说 (shuō, say) and 就 (jiù, then immediately). It means doing something the moment it is mentioned, without hesitation. Pattern: 说 + verb + 就 + same verb.

name: 固定短语
title: Expression 不得了
explanation: 不得了 (bùdéliǎo) means 'extremely' or 'terrible, serious'. After an adjective or feeling verb it works as a degree complement: Adjective/verb + 得 (de, links to the result) + 不得了. It can also stand alone to say a situation is serious.

name: 固定短语
title: No need to: 用不着
explanation: 用不着 (yòng bu zháo, no need to; have no use for) says that something is unnecessary. It goes before a verb or noun: Subject + 用不着 + verb/object.

name: 固定短语
title: Judging from: 从……来看
explanation: 从……来看 (cóng … lái kàn, judging from; from the point of view of) wraps around the basis for an opinion: 从 (cóng, from) + basis + 来看 (lái kàn, to look at it), + conclusion. The conclusion follows the phrase.

name: 固定短语
title: Each does their own: A的A，B的B
explanation: Pattern: A + 的 (de, particle linking the parts) + A, B + 的 + B, where A and B are two different verbs or words. It paints a lively scene in which some people do one thing and others do another.

name: 固定短语
title: Ever since: （自）……以来
explanation: （自）……以来 (zì … yǐlái, since) marks a period from a past point up to now. Pattern: (自 zì, from) + time or event + 以来 (yǐlái, since then), + what has happened during that period. 自 can be left out.

name: 固定短语
title: Be made up of: 由……组成
explanation: 由……组成 (yóu … zǔchéng, be made up of; be composed of) names the parts that form a whole. Pattern: Whole + 由 (yóu, by; from) + parts + 组成 (zǔchéng, to compose).

name: 固定短语
title: Neither this nor that: X也不是，Y也不是
explanation: Pattern: X + 也不是 (yě bú shì, is not either), Y + 也不是. X and Y are usually two opposite options, such as two actions. The phrase says that neither is right, which leaves the person in an awkward spot or at a loss.

name: 固定短语
title: Can neither X nor Y: X也X不得，Y也Y不得
explanation: Pattern: Verb X + 也 (yě, also) + X + 不得 (bu dé, cannot; must not), Verb Y + 也 + Y + 不得. It describes a dilemma in which someone can do neither of two things, or is stuck. The verbs are repeated, and X and Y are often opposites.

title: It's all down to it: X是它，Y也是它
explanation: Pattern: X + 是 (shì, be) + 它 (tā, it), Y + 也 (yě, also) + 是 + 它. X and Y are different situations or uses, and 它 points back to one same thing. The point is that this one thing accounts for or does all of them.

title: Might as well: X着也是X着
explanation: Pattern: Verb + 着 (zhe, marks a continuing state) + 也是 (yě shì, is also; anyway) + the same verb + 着. It means "since it is happening anyway" and is followed by a suggestion to make some use of the situation.

title: In any case: 不管怎样说
explanation: 不管怎样说 (bùguǎn zěnyàng shuō, however you put it; in any case) is an opening phrase. It is made of 不管 (bùguǎn, no matter), 怎样 (zěnyàng, how) and 说 (shuō, to say). It introduces a conclusion that holds whatever else is true.

title: You really are something: 真有你/他/她的
explanation: 真有 (zhēn yǒu, really have) + 你 (nǐ, you) / 他 (tā, he) / 她 (tā, she) + 的 (de, particle). It is an exclamation about someone's behavior. Depending on tone and context, it means admiration ("you're amazing") or exasperation ("you're something else").

title: Dismissive repeat: X什么X
explanation: Pattern: Verb or adjective X + 什么 (shénme, what) + the same X. It is a pushback that means "why bother with X?" or "no need to X". It sounds impatient or critical.

title: Brushing aside a question: 什么X不X（的）
explanation: Pattern: 什么 (shénme, what) + X + 不 (bù, not) + X + optional 的 (de, particle). X is a verb or adjective. It brushes the matter aside, as in "never mind whether it's X or not".

title: Might as well, it's free: 不X白不X
explanation: Pattern: 不 (bù, not) + Verb + 白 (bái, in vain; for nothing) + 不 + the same verb. It means "if you don't do X, you've wasted the chance", so you may as well do it while you can, often when it costs nothing.

title: Over and over: X来X去，都是/就是……
explanation: Pattern: Verb + 来 (lái, come) + the same verb + 去 (qù, go), then 都是 (dōu shì, are all) or 就是 (jiù shì, is just) + conclusion. The first part describes doing something again and again or back and forth. The second part gives the result: after all that, it all comes down to this.

title: Whatever it is: Verb + 什么（就）是什么
explanation: Pattern: Verb + 什么 (shénme, what; whatever) + (就 jiù, then) + 是 (shì, be) + 什么. The second 什么 points back to the first. It means "whatever it turns out to be, that's what it is", showing that someone accepts what is available and isn't picky.

name: 状语
title: Several adverbials in one sentence
explanation: An adverbial is a word or phrase before the verb or adjective that says when, where or how. A sentence can stack several, usually in this order: Subject + time + adverbs (such as 也 yě, also; 都 dōu, all) + place or other phrases + manner + verb. The more a modifier describes the action itself, the closer it sits to the verb.

name: 补语
title: Can / cannot with 得 and 不得
explanation: Pattern: Verb + 得 (de, can be done) or Verb + 不得 (bu dé, cannot be done; must not). The 不得 form often means "must not" or "is not allowed", and both forms are often fixed, formal expressions.

name: 补语
content: 形容词/心理动词+得+不得了
title: Extremely: ……得不得了
explanation: Pattern: Adjective or verb of feeling/thinking + 得 (de, particle linking to the degree) + 不得了 (bù déliǎo, extremely; terribly). It says the quality or feeling is extreme.

name: 补语
content: 趋向补语的引申用法：表示状态意义：动词/形容词+下来/下去/起来/过来/过去
title: Figurative direction endings showing a state
explanation: After a verb or adjective, 下来 (xiàlái), 下去 (xiàqù), 起来 (qǐlái), 过来 (guòlái) and 过去 (guòqù) stop describing movement and describe a state or change. Roughly: 下来 means settling down or continuing up to now; 下去 means continuing into the future; 起来 means starting; 过来 means returning to normal; 过去 means passing out or drifting away from normal.

name: 补语
title: Description after 得: a verb phrase
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb/adjective + 得 (de, particle linking to the result or degree) + verb phrase. What follows 得 is an action (a verb with its object or other parts) that shows how far or in what way the first verb or adjective goes.

name: 补语
title: Description after 得: a full clause
explanation: Pattern: Subject + verb/adjective + 得 (de, particle linking to the result or degree) + new subject + predicate. What follows 得 is a small sentence with its own subject. It shows the result of the first part, as in "so much that something happens".

name: 补语
title: Description after 得: a set phrase
explanation: Pattern: Verb/adjective + 得 (de, particle linking to the result or degree) + set phrase. The set phrase is a ready-made expression such as a four-character idiom, and it vividly describes the degree or manner.

name: 特殊句型
content: （1）表示存在、具有：主语+有+着+宾语
title: 有着: formal "has" or "there is"
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 有 (yǒu, have; there is) + 着 (zhe, marks a continuing state) + object. It is a rather formal or written way to say that something exists or that someone possesses something, often an abstract thing. 着 adds a sense of lasting state.

name: 特殊句型
title: Verb + 有: something attached
explanation: Pattern: Subject (often a place or surface) + verb + 有 (yǒu, have) + object. Here 有 works like 着 (zhe, continuing state) and tells what has been put on, written on or attached to the subject. The verb is usually something like writing, carving or hanging.

name: 特殊句型
title: The 把 construction with 一 before the verb
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, takes the object and acts on it) + object + 一 (yī, one) + verb. The 一 before the verb presents the action as a single quick move, often with a result or a following action that comes right after.

name: 特殊句型
title: The 把 construction with two objects
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, takes the object and acts on it) + object 1 + verb + object 2. Object 1 is the thing being handled. Object 2 after the verb is a second item, such as the person receiving it or what object 1 becomes.

name: 特殊句型
content: 前后两个动词性词语具有因果、转折、条件关系
title: Verb chains showing cause, contrast or condition
explanation: Two verb phrases follow one subject with no linking word between them. Unlike a simple sequence of actions, the second verb phrase is the result of the first, goes against what you would expect from the first, or happens only under the condition the first sets. You work out which relationship it is from the meaning.

name: 特殊句型
title: Comparison with an amount of difference
explanation: Pattern: A + adjective + B + amount (number + measure word, or a word like 一点儿 or 多了). It says A is more than B in that quality, and the amount tells you by how much.

name: 特殊句型
content: 主语+被/叫/让+宾语+给+动词+其他成分
title: Passive sentences with 被, 叫, 让 and 给
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 被 (bèi) / 叫 (jiào) / 让 (ràng) + doer + 给 (gěi) + verb + other element. The subject is the one that receives the action, and 被, 叫 and 让 all mean by. The 给 before the verb is an optional extra word that adds emphasis and has no separate meaning here, and the doer can sometimes be left out.

name: 复句
title: Then, in sequence, with 便
explanation: Pattern: Clause 1, 便 (biàn, then) + clause 2. 便 is a formal, written word like 就 (jiù, then). It shows that the second event follows right after the first.

name: 复句
title: Either…or… with 或是
explanation: Pattern: 或是 (huòshì, or) + option 1, 或是 + option 2. It lists alternatives, meaning either this or that, and the options may be more than two.

name: 复句
title: Once…then… with 一旦…就…
explanation: Pattern: 一旦 (yídàn, once, if ever) + situation, 就 (jiù, then) + result. It says that if the situation ever happens, the result follows right away. The situation is often something important or unwelcome.

name: 复句
title: If…then… with 假如
explanation: Pattern: 假如 (jiǎrú, if) + supposed situation, (就 jiù, then) + result. It sets up an imagined condition and then says what follows. The 就 is optional.

name: 复句
title: In case… with 万一
explanation: Pattern: 万一 (wànyī, in case, if by any chance) + unlikely situation, (就 jiù, then) + result. It introduces a possibility that is very unlikely and usually unwanted. The 就 is optional.

name: 复句
title: Otherwise, with 要不然 and 不然
explanation: Pattern: Clause 1, 要不然 (yàobùrán, otherwise) / 不然 (bùrán, otherwise) + clause 2. Clause 1 states what is or should be the case. Clause 2 says what would happen if it were not so, and the two forms mean the same.

name: 复句
title: Therefore, with 因而
explanation: Pattern: Cause, 因而 (yīn'ér, therefore, and so) + result. It is a fairly formal, written link where the first part gives the reason and the part after 因而 gives the outcome.

name: 复句
title: It shows that…, with 可见
explanation: Pattern: Evidence, 可见 (kějiàn, so it can be seen that) + conclusion. The first part gives a fact, and what follows 可见 is the conclusion drawn from it.

name: 复句
title: Even if…still… with 哪怕…也…
explanation: Pattern: 哪怕 (nǎpà, even if) + extreme situation, 也 (yě, still) + result. It says the result stays the same even in the extreme case named after 哪怕.

name: 复句
title: Not only not…but instead… with 不但不 and 反而
explanation: Pattern: 不但不 (búdàn bù, not only not) / 不但没有 (búdàn méiyǒu, not only did not) + expected thing, 反而 (fǎn'ér, on the contrary, instead) + opposite or surprising thing. The expected result did not happen, and something contrary to it happened instead.

name: 复句
title: Not…, and also or still…, with 不是…还/还是…
explanation: Pattern: 不是 (búshì, is not) + first part, 还 (hái, in addition, even more) / 还是 (háishì, still, all the same) + second part. The first part denies or sets aside something, and the second part goes a step further or points to what holds anyway.

name: 复句
title: The purpose is…, with 为的是
explanation: Pattern: Action, 为的是 (wèi de shì, the aim is to) + purpose. The first part says what is done, and the part after 为的是 says the goal it serves.

name: 复句
title: Without…there is no…
explanation: Pattern: 没有 (méiyǒu, without, not have) + thing, 就 (jiù, then) 没有 + result. The two halves are run together with no pause. It says the first thing is necessary for the second to exist.

name: 复句
title: If not…then not… with a repeated 不
explanation: Pattern: 不 (bù, not) + verb or phrase, 不 + verb or phrase. The two short halves are packed together with no connecting word. It reads as if you don't do the first, the second won't happen, so the first is required.

name: 复句
title: No matter how…still… with 再…也…
explanation: Pattern: 再 (zài, more, to a greater degree) + adjective or verb, 也 (yě, still) + result. It says that even to an extreme degree, the result does not change.

name: 类前缀
title: Prefixes that attach to the front of a word
explanation: These small word-parts go before a word and change its meaning: 超 (chāo, super, ultra), 多 (duō, multi-, many), 反 (fǎn, anti-, counter-), 无 (wú, without, non-), 亚 (yà, sub-, secondary), 准 (zhǔn, quasi-, nearly, semi-). Spot them at the start of a longer word and read the rest as the base meaning.

name: 类后缀
title: Suffixes that attach to the end of a word
explanation: These small word-parts go after a word to build a new one: 化 (huà, -ize, becoming), 式 (shì, -style, -type), 型 (xíng, -type, model), 性 (xìng, -ness, -ity, a quality). Spot them at the end of a word and read what comes before as the base meaning.

name: 代词
title: The pronoun 人家
explanation: 人家 (rénjia, other people, he/she/they) refers to a person or people other than the speaker and listener, or to someone just mentioned. In casual speech, especially from women, it can also mean I or me with a playful or complaining tone.

name: 量词
content: 专用名量词：串、滴、枝、扇、卷1、卷2
title: Specific measure words for nouns
explanation: Pattern: Number + measure word + noun. These measure words go with particular kinds of things: 串 (chuàn, a string or bunch), 滴 (dī, a drop), 枝 (zhī, a stick-like thing such as a flower or pen), 扇 (shàn, a door or window panel), 卷 (juǎn, a roll, as of paper or film) and 卷 (juàn, a volume, scroll or exam paper). The same character 卷 has two readings, and the reading tells you which measure word it is.

name: 量词
title: The action measure word 番
explanation: Pattern: Verb + number + 番 (fān, a round, a time, an occasion). It counts how many times an action is done and is used for actions that take effort, time or thought. A common form is 一番 (yì fān, one round), which suggests the action was done thoroughly.

name: 副词
title: Degree adverbs (advanced)
explanation: These adverbs go before an adjective or feeling verb to say how strong it is: 特 (tè, especially, very), 异常 (yìcháng, unusually, extremely) and 较为 (jiàowéi, relatively, fairly). Pattern: Subject + degree adverb + adjective.

name: 副词
title: Adverbs of scope
explanation: These adverbs go before the verb and say who or what an action covers: 净 (jìng, only, nothing but), 一同 (yìtóng, together) and 大都 (dàdōu, mostly, for the most part). Pattern: Subject + adverb + verb.

name: 副词
content: 一时、不时、仍旧、依旧、一向
title: Adverbs of time
explanation: These adverbs go before the verb and say when or for how long something happens: 一时 (yìshí, for the moment, temporarily), 不时 (bùshí, from time to time), 仍旧 (réngjiù, still), 依旧 (yījiù, still, as before) and 一向 (yíxiàng, all along, always until now).

name: 副词
title: Adverbs of frequency
explanation: These adverbs go before a verb and say that an action is repeated: 一再 (yízài, again and again) and 再三 (zàisān, over and over, repeatedly). Pattern: Subject + adverb + verb.

name: 副词
content: 不禁、赶忙、特地、特意、偷偷
title: Adverbs of manner
explanation: These adverbs go before a verb and describe how or why someone does something: 不禁 (bùjīn, can't help but), 赶忙 (gǎnmáng, hurriedly), 特地 (tèdì, specially, on purpose), 特意 (tèyì, deliberately, specially) and 偷偷 (tōutōu, secretly).

name: 副词
title: Negative adverb 未必
explanation: 未必 (wèibì, not necessarily, may not) goes before a verb or adjective and softens a claim: it says something is not certain to be true, rather than flatly denying it. Pattern: Subject + 未必 + verb/adjective.

name: 副词
content: 恰好、倒是、干脆、明明、总算
title: Adverbs of attitude
explanation: These adverbs show the speaker's attitude toward what is said: 恰好 (qiàhǎo, happening to fit perfectly), 倒是 (dàoshì, actually, on the contrary; a mild contrast), 干脆 (gāncuì, simply, might as well), 明明 (míngmíng, obviously, though the facts are ignored or contradicted) and 总算 (zǒngsuàn, finally, at long last). They usually come before the verb.

name: 介词
title: Preposition 于 for time and place
explanation: 于 (yú, at, in, on) is a formal, written preposition that introduces a time or a place. Pattern: Verb + 于 + time/place, or Subject + 于 + time/place + verb.

name: 介词
title: Introducing a topic with 至于
explanation: 至于 (zhìyú, as for, as to) introduces a new person or matter that the speaker now turns to. Pattern: 至于 + topic, + comment about it.

name: 介词
title: Preposition 因 for reason or purpose
explanation: 因 (yīn, because of, due to) is a formal preposition that introduces the cause or reason for something. Pattern: 因 + reason, + result.

name: 介词
title: Preposition 除 for exclusion
explanation: 除 (chú, except, apart from) introduces the thing that is set aside from the rest. It is often closed by a word such as 外 (wài, outside), and whether the sentence means 'except' or 'besides' depends on what follows. Pattern: 除 + thing set aside + (外), + the rest.

name: 连词
title: Conjunction 不料 for unexpected turns
explanation: 不料 (búliào, unexpectedly, who would have thought) begins a second clause that describes something surprising, contrary to what the first clause led you to expect. Pattern: Clause 1, + 不料 + surprising clause 2.

name: 助词
title: Particle 所 before a verb
explanation: 所 (suǒ) is a formal particle placed before a verb to turn it into a 'that which is verbed' phrase. It often appears in the pattern 所 + verb + 的 (de, the marker linking a description to its noun).

name: 助词
title: Sentence-final particles 啦 and 嘛
explanation: 啦 (la) goes at the end of a sentence and adds a lively tone, often showing a new situation or excitement. 嘛 (ma) goes at the end and suggests that something is obvious or should be clear, or adds a note of persuasion.

name: 助词
title: Particle 也好 for 'whether... or...'
explanation: 也好 (yěhǎo) is used after each of two or more options to mean that it makes no difference which one applies. Pattern: A + 也好, + B + 也好, + the result that stays the same.

name: 固定短语
title: Fixed pattern A这A那
explanation: The pattern repeats one word A (usually a verb) with 这 (zhè, this) and 那 (nà, that) between the repeats, to describe going on and on about this and that. Pattern: A + 这 + A + 那.

name: 固定短语
title: Fixed pattern 左A右B
explanation: The pattern puts 左 (zuǒ, left) and 右 (yòu, right) before two matching or related words, to say that something is done again and again or from every direction. Pattern: 左 + A + 右 + B.

name: 固定短语
title: 好(不)容易 for 'with great difficulty'
explanation: 好容易 and 好不容易 (hǎo(bù)róngyì, with great difficulty, finally managed) mean the same thing, even though one has 不 (bù, not) and the other does not. They say something was hard to achieve but did happen in the end. The parts are 好 (hǎo, very) and 容易 (róngyì, easy).

name: 固定短语
title: Conceding with 那倒(也)是
explanation: 那倒(也)是 (nà dào (yě) shì, that's true, I suppose) is a set phrase used to agree with what someone has said, often after having doubted it. The parts are 那 (nà, that), 倒 (dào, indeed), 也 (yě, also) and 是 (shì, is so); the 也 can be left out.

name: 固定短语
title: Dropping a matter with 算了
explanation: 算了 (suànle, forget it, let it go) is said to give up on something, end an argument, or tell someone not to bother. It comes from 算 (suàn, to count as) and 了 (le, a particle marking completion), and usually stands alone as a short sentence.

name: 固定短语
title: Stopping someone with 得了
explanation: 得了 (déle, enough, that'll do, come on) is a short exclamation used to cut someone off, refuse something, or show impatience. It is said on its own and is a different word from the 得了 that means 'can be done'.

title: Parallel pattern A一+measure word, B一+measure word
explanation: Two parts of the same shape sit side by side, each made of a word plus 一 (yī, one) plus a measure word, to show things matched up one by one or following one after another. Pattern: A + 一 + measure word, + B + 一 + measure word.

title: Scattered-pattern 东一A,西一A
explanation: The pattern uses 东 (dōng, east) and 西 (xī, west) with 一 (yī, one) and a repeated word A, to describe things scattered here and there or done in a haphazard way. Pattern: 东 + 一 + A, + 西 + 一 + A.

title: Pattern 到……为止 for 'up to, until'
explanation: The pattern wraps a time or point between 到 (dào, until, up to) and 为止 (wéizhǐ, as the stopping point) to say that something lasts or counts up to that limit and stops there. Pattern: 到 + time/point + 为止, + what happens up to then.

title: Pattern X到Y头上来了
explanation: Literally 'X has come onto Y's head', it means that something, usually unpleasant like trouble or a burden, has now landed on Y. The parts are 到 (dào, to, onto), 头上 (tóu shang, on the head) and 来了 (lái le, has come). Pattern: X (the matter) + 到 + Y (the person) + 头上来了.

title: Not X not…, as soon as X…
explanation: Pattern: 不 (bù, not) + Verb + 不 (bù, not) + Clause, 一 (yī, once, as soon as) + same Verb + Clause. The same verb appears twice: the first half says that without doing the action you won't notice or know something, and the second half says that the moment you do it, something surprising or striking appears.

title: Scolding with 好你个…
explanation: Pattern: 好 (hǎo, well, good) + 你 (nǐ, you) + 个 (gè, a general measure word) + Noun. It is an exclamation of anger or indignation aimed at someone, like 'Well, you...!' or 'Good grief, you...!', and the noun names what the speaker accuses them of being. It is sometimes used playfully.

title: Neither earlier nor later (bad timing)
explanation: Pattern: 早 (zǎo, early) + (也 yě, even) + 不 (bù, not) + Verb, 晚 (wǎn, late) + (也 yě, even) + 不 (bù, not) + Verb. It means 'not sooner, not later', and complains that something happens at exactly the wrong moment. The 也 is optional, and the sentence goes on to say what happened at that inconvenient time.

title: Look how… (看/瞧 + 把 sentences)
explanation: Pattern: 看 (kàn, look) or 瞧 (qiáo, look) + 把 (bǎ, a word that puts the following noun up front) + Person + Verb/Adjective + 得 (de, links a verb to its result) + Result. It comments on the state someone has got into, as in 'Look at how worked up you are!'. The person right after 把 is the one who is in that state.

title: Leaving X there but not doing Y
explanation: Pattern: 放着 (fàngzhe, having something sitting there) + Noun X + 不 (bù, not) + Verb Y. It criticizes someone for having a thing available and yet not using it or doing the obvious thing with it, which is seen as a waste or as foolish.

title: What's done is done (X了就X了)
explanation: Pattern: Verb + 了 (le, marks completion) + 就 (jiù, then, just) + same Verb + 了, followed by (没)有 (méi yǒu, there is not / yǒu, there is) + something. It means 'so it happened, so what', and the next part is usually a remark that it is no big deal, or that there is nothing worth worrying about.

title: This isn't…, that isn't… (finding fault with everything)
explanation: Pattern: 这 (zhè, this) + 也 (yě, also, even) + 不 (bù, not) + X, 那 (nà, that) + 也 (yě, also, even) + 不 (bù, not) + Y. The order of 这 and 那 can be swapped. It expresses that nothing is acceptable, whether the speaker is being picky or is stuck because every option seems wrong.

title: X is X, Y is Y (keeping things separate)
explanation: Pattern: X + 归 (guī, belongs to, is counted as) + X, Y + 归 (guī) + Y. It says two matters should be kept apart and not mixed up, as in 'business is business, friendship is friendship'. The same word may be repeated on each side of 归, or two different words may be used.

title: Look at you…! (看你X的 / 瞧他X的)
explanation: Pattern: 看 (kàn, look) or 瞧 (qiáo, look) + 你 (nǐ, you) or 他 (tā, he, him) + Adjective/Verb phrase + 的 (de, closing particle). It is an exclamation of teasing, scolding or sympathy about how someone looks or behaves, as in 'Look at you, all...!'. Other people can replace 你 or 他.

name: 补语
title: Extreme degree with 透了
explanation: Pattern: Verb/Adjective + 透 (tòu, through, thoroughly) + 了 (le, particle marking a state). It says the action or quality has reached an extreme, 'thoroughly' or 'utterly', and is most often used for unpleasant feelings or conditions.

name: 特殊句型
content: （1）主语（非生物体）+把+宾语+动词+其他成分
title: 把 sentences with a non-living subject
explanation: Pattern: Subject (a thing or event, not a person) + 把 (bǎ, takes the object and acts on it) + Object + Verb + Other element (such as a result or direction). The subject is something like weather or an event that causes a change to the object, and the verb is followed by something that says what happened.

name: 特殊句型
content: （2）主语+把+宾语（施事）+动词+其他成分
title: 把 sentences where the object is the doer
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 把 (bǎ, takes the object and acts on it) + Object + Verb + Other element. Here the noun after 把 is the one performing the verb rather than receiving it. This often suggests that the action has an unwelcome effect on the subject, so don't read it as 'the subject does the verb to the object'.

name: 复句
title: One moment…, the next moment…
explanation: Pattern: 一时 (yīshí, for a moment, at one time) + Situation A, 一时 (yīshí) + Situation B. It describes things changing back and forth in quick succession, such as moods or conditions that keep shifting.

name: 复句
title: Either…, or…
explanation: Pattern: 要么 (yàome, either, or else) + Option A, 要么 (yàome) + Option B. It presents two alternatives and says one of them has to be chosen.

name: 复句
title: Although…, but…
explanation: Pattern: 虽 (suī, although; short for 虽然) + Clause A, 但 (dàn, but) / 可 (kě, but) / 却 (què, yet) / 也 (yě, still) + Clause B. The first clause admits a fact, and the second gives a contrasting point. Normally you use just one of the four connecting words in the second clause.

name: 复句
title: Every… without exception
explanation: Pattern: 凡是 (fánshì, any, every, whatever) + Category, 都 (dōu, all) + Result. It says that everything or everyone falling into the category shares the same result, with no exceptions.

name: 复句
title: Only if… (除非…才…)
explanation: Pattern: 除非 (chúfēi, unless, only if) + Condition, 才 (cái, only then) + Result. The result happens only when the condition is met, and in no other case.

name: 复句
title: Unless…, otherwise… (除非…否则/不然…)
explanation: Pattern: 除非 (chúfēi, unless) + Condition, 否则 (fǒuzé, otherwise) / 不然 (bùrán, otherwise) + Consequence. The first part names what must happen, and the second part says what will happen if it doesn't, usually something unwanted.

name: 复句
title: Even if… (就算…也…)
explanation: Pattern: 就算 (jiùsuàn, even if) + Hypothetical situation, 也 (yě, still, even so) + Result. It says the result stays the same even in the worst or most extreme case imagined in the first part.

name: 复句
title: So that… (…，以便…)
explanation: Pattern: Clause (an action or arrangement), 以便 (yǐbiàn, so that, in order to) + Purpose. The second part gives the goal that the first part makes easier or possible.

name: 类前缀
title: Prefix-like elements 后— and 亲—
explanation: These are word pieces placed at the start of a longer word to add meaning. 后 (hòu, after, back, later) points to something later or at the rear, and 亲 (qīn, close, related, personal) adds the idea of closeness, family ties or being friendly toward something.

name: 类后缀
title: Suffix-like elements —观, —鬼, —界, —然, —坛, —为, —制
explanation: These are word pieces added to the end of a word to form a new term. 观 (guān) means a view or outlook, 鬼 (guǐ, ghost) names a person with a bad habit, often mockingly, 界 (jiè) a field or circle of people, 然 (rán) a state or manner like 'in that way', 坛 (tán) the arena of a field such as sports or literature, 为 (wéi) 'to be, as', and 制 (zhì) a system or the way something is made or run.

name: 动词
content: 巴不得、并非、除外、犯不着、犯得着、恨不得、可否、可谓、免不了、所谓、有所、予以
title: Set verbs and verb-like expressions
explanation: These are fixed expressions, mostly used as verbs, that you learn as single units: 巴不得 (bābude, be eager to, can't wait), 恨不得 (hènbude, wish one could), 并非 (bìngfēi, is by no means), 除外 (chúwài, excepted), 犯不着 (fànbuzháo, not worth it), 犯得着 (fàndezháo, worth the trouble), and 可否 (kěfǒu, may or may not, is it permissible). Also: 可谓 (kěwèi, can be called), 免不了 (miǎnbuliǎo, unavoidable), 所谓 (suǒwèi, so-called), 有所 (yǒusuǒ, to some degree, placed before a verb), and 予以 (yǔyǐ, to give or carry out, placed before a formal verb).

name: 代词
title: The pronoun 我 in fixed uses
explanation: Beyond its basic meaning 我 (wǒ, I, me), it appears inside words and set phrases to mean 'my', 'our' or 'oneself'. Watch for it attached straight to a noun with no 的 (de, possessive particle) to mean 'our' or 'my own side'.

name: 代词
title: Formal and colloquial pointing words 彼, 这么着, 兹
explanation: These are demonstratives, words that point to things. 彼 (bǐ, that, the other) is literary and contrasts with 此 (cǐ, this); 兹 (zī, this, now) is formal and appears in notices and official writing; 这么着 (zhèmezhe, like this, in that case) is colloquial and refers to a way of doing something or to a situation just mentioned.

name: 代词
title: Formal and casual question words 何 and 怎么着
explanation: 何 (hé, what / which / why) is a formal, written-style question word that combines with other words rather than standing alone. 怎么着 (zěnmezhe, do what / how about it / whatever) is a casual spoken phrase used as a question about what to do or how things should go.

name: 代词
title: Indefinite amount with 若干
explanation: 若干 (ruògān, several / a certain number of) refers to an amount that is unspecified or not worth stating. It goes before a noun, sometimes with a measure word between: "若干 + (measure word) + noun".

name: 量词
content: 重、截、缕、码、枚、摊、丸、则、幢、宗
title: Less common measure words for nouns
explanation: These measure words go between a number and a noun: "Number + measure word + noun". 重 (chóng, layer or tier), 截 (jié, a cut-off section), 缕 (lǚ, a wisp or strand), 码 (mǎ, a matter or affair), 枚 (méi, a small item such as a coin, medal or stamp), 摊 (tān, a puddle or a spread-out heap), 丸 (wán, a pill or pellet), 则 (zé, an item of text such as a news piece or short passage), 幢 (zhuàng, a building) and 宗 (zōng, a case, deal or batch).

name: 量词
title: Action measure word 通
explanation: 通 (tòng, a spell or bout) counts an action that happens once through, such as a burst of talking or scolding. Pattern: "Verb + number + 通 (+ object)".

name: 量词
title: Compound measure word 人次
explanation: 人次 (réncì, person-times) counts the total number of attendances or visits, with each person counted every time they come. It follows a number: "Number + 人次".

name: 副词
content: 大为、分外、何等、极度、极力、略、略微、颇、稍稍、万分、微、尤为、愈加、越发
title: Degree adverbs (advanced)
explanation: Degree adverbs go before an adjective or verb to say how strong or how slight something is: "Subject + degree adverb + adjective/verb". Strong or increasing: 大为 (dàwéi, greatly), 分外 (fènwài, especially), 何等 (héděng, how / what a), 极度 (jídù, extremely), 极力 (jílì, to the utmost), 颇 (pō, quite), 万分 (wànfēn, extremely), 尤为 (yóuwéi, especially), 愈加 (yùjiā, even more) and 越发 (yuèfā, increasingly). Slight: 略 (lüè, slightly), 略微 (lüèwēi, slightly), 稍稍 (shāoshāo, a little) and 微 (wēi, slightly).

name: 副词
content: 大体、概、皆、尽、均、通通、统统、唯、唯独、唯有、无非、一概
title: Scope adverbs (advanced)
explanation: These adverbs go before the verb and say how many or how much is covered. Meaning all or without exception: 皆 (jiē, all), 尽 (jǐn, all), 均 (jūn, all / equally), 通通 (tōngtōng, all), 统统 (tǒngtǒng, all), 一概 (yígài, without exception) and 概 (gài, without exception, often with a negative). Meaning mostly: 大体 (dàtǐ, by and large). Meaning only: 唯 (wéi, only), 唯独 (wéidú, only / alone), 唯有 (wéiyǒu, only) and 无非 (wúfēi, nothing but).

name: 副词
content: 姑且、即、即时、届时、尽早、就此、历来、尚、随即、向来、一经、暂且、早日
title: Time adverbs (advanced)
explanation: These adverbs go before the verb and place an action in time. Immediately or soon: 即 (jí, immediately), 即时 (jíshí, immediately), 随即 (suíjí, right afterward), 一经 (yìjīng, as soon as / once), 尽早 (jǐnzǎo, as early as possible), 早日 (zǎorì, soon) and 届时 (jièshí, when that time comes). Temporary or ongoing: 姑且 (gūqiě, for the time being), 暂且 (zànqiě, for now), 尚 (shàng, still / yet), 历来 (lìlái, always, all along) and 向来 (xiànglái, always up to now). Also 就此 (jiùcǐ, at this point / hereby).

name: 副词
content: 连连、屡次、屡屡、频、时而、时时、相继、一个劲（儿）、一连、再度
title: Frequency adverbs (advanced)
explanation: These adverbs go before the verb and say that an action repeats or keeps going. 连连 (liánlián, repeatedly), 屡次 (lǚcì, many times), 屡屡 (lǚlǚ, over and over), 频 (pín, frequently), 时时 (shíshí, often), 一连 (yìlián, in a row), 相继 (xiāngjì, one after another), 一个劲（儿） (yí gè jìn(r), keep on nonstop) and 再度 (zàidù, once again). 时而 (shí'ér, from time to time) is often used twice to mean "now this, now that".

name: 副词
content: 按理、按说、百般、不由得、趁机、趁早、大肆、断然、公然、火速、截然、竭力、尽情、就近、刻意、拼命、强行、任意、日趋、如期、擅自、私自、特此、瞎、一并、一举、一手、毅然、有意、照常、照例、照样、执意、骤然、逐一、专程
title: Manner adverbs (advanced)
explanation: These adverbs go before a verb and describe how or why the action is done. Attitude or effort: 百般 (bǎibān, in every way), 大肆 (dàsì, without restraint), 断然 (duànrán, resolutely), 毅然 (yìrán, resolutely), 公然 (gōngrán, openly), 竭力 (jiélì, doing one's utmost), 拼命 (pīnmìng, desperately), 尽情 (jìnqíng, to one's heart's content), 刻意 (kèyì, deliberately), 有意 (yǒuyì, intentionally), 执意 (zhíyì, insisting on), 强行 (qiángxíng, by force), 任意 (rènyì, arbitrarily), 擅自 (shànzì, without authorization), 私自 (sīzì, privately), 瞎 (xiā, blindly) and 专程 (zhuānchéng, on a special trip). Speed, timing or sequence: 火速 (huǒsù, at top speed), 骤然 (zhòurán, suddenly), 趁机 (chènjī, taking the opportunity), 趁早 (chènzǎo, while it is early), 如期 (rúqī, on schedule), 日趋 (rìqū, increasingly day by day), 一举 (yìjǔ, in one move), 一手 (yìshǒu, single-handedly), 一并 (yíbìng, together), 逐一 (zhúyī, one by one), 就近 (jiùjìn, nearby) and 截然 (jiérán, sharply, as in clearly different). Expectation and routine: 按理 (ànlǐ, by rights), 按说 (ànshuō, normally speaking), 不由得 (bùyóude, can't help but), 照常 (zhàocháng, as usual), 照例 (zhàolì, as a rule), 照样 (zhàoyàng, all the same) and 特此 (tècǐ, hereby).

name: 副词
content: 不见得、绝不、无从、无须、无可、勿
title: Negative adverbs (advanced)
explanation: These words go before a verb to negate it in a particular way: "Subject + negative adverb + verb". 不见得 (bújiàndé, not necessarily), 绝不 (juébù, absolutely not), 无从 (wúcóng, have no way to), 无须 (wúxū, no need to), 无可 (wúkě, nothing to be done / cannot) and 勿 (wù, don't, used in formal prohibitions).

name: 副词
content: 必定、必将、不妨、不免、反倒、非得、分明、怪不得、果真、好在、何必、竟、愣、莫非、难怪、宁可、宁愿、碰巧、偏偏、恰巧、切、情愿、势必、索性、万万、未免、务必、幸好、幸亏、终究、何不、何尝、何苦
title: Attitude adverbs (advanced)
explanation: These adverbs go before the verb or at the start of a clause and show the speaker's stance. Certainty or necessity: 必定 (bìdìng, surely), 必将 (bìjiāng, will certainly), 势必 (shìbì, bound to), 务必 (wùbì, must), 万万 (wànwàn, absolutely), 切 (qiè, by all means), 非得 (fēiděi, must), 分明 (fēnmíng, clearly) and 终究 (zhōngjiū, in the end). Surprise or contrary to expectation: 竟 (jìng, unexpectedly), 愣 (lèng, unexpectedly / stubbornly), 反倒 (fǎndào, on the contrary), 偏偏 (piānpiān, contrary to what was wanted), 果真 (guǒzhēn, sure enough), 莫非 (mòfēi, could it be that), 未免 (wèimiǎn, a bit too much), 不免 (bùmiǎn, inevitably), 怪不得 (guàibude, no wonder) and 难怪 (nánguài, no wonder). Luck, choice and rhetorical questions: 好在 (hǎozài, fortunately), 幸好 (xìnghǎo, luckily), 幸亏 (xìngkuī, luckily), 碰巧 (pèngqiǎo, by chance), 恰巧 (qiàqiǎo, happen to), 宁可 (nìngkě, would rather), 宁愿 (nìngyuàn, would rather), 情愿 (qíngyuàn, would rather), 不妨 (bùfáng, might as well), 索性 (suǒxìng, simply), 何必 (hébì, why bother), 何不 (hébù, why not), 何苦 (hékǔ, why go to the trouble) and 何尝 (hécháng, not at all, as a rhetorical question).

name: 副词
title: Formal 'to be' with 乃
explanation: 乃 (nǎi, to be) is a formal, written-style word that links a subject to what it is: "Subject + 乃 + noun". It does the job of 是 (shì, to be) in classical-flavored writing.

name: 介词
title: Preposition 打 meaning 'from'
explanation: 打 (dǎ, from) is a casual spoken preposition that introduces the starting time or place of an action: "打 + time/place + verb". It works like 从 (cóng, from).

name: 介词
title: Prepositions that introduce a target: 当着 and 就
explanation: 当着 (dāngzhe, in the presence of) introduces the person in front of whom something is done: "当着 + person + verb phrase". 就 (jiù, regarding / with respect to) introduces the topic being discussed or judged: "就 + topic + comment".

name: 介词
title: Prepositions for basis or grounds
explanation: These introduce the principle, reason or standard that an action is based on: "Preposition + basis, main clause". 本着 (běnzhe, in line with a principle), 基于 (jīyú, based on), 鉴于 (jiànyú, in view of), 经 (jīng, through / after going through) and 依 (yī, according to).

name: 连词
content: 鉴于2、况且、免得、若、倘若、以防
title: Conjunctions linking clauses (advanced)
explanation: These words join two clauses or sentences and show how they relate. Reason or addition: 鉴于 (jiànyú, given that) and 况且 (kuàngqiě, besides / moreover). Condition: 若 (ruò, if) and 倘若 (tǎngruò, if). Purpose or prevention: 免得 (miǎnde, so as not to) and 以防 (yǐfáng, in case / to guard against).

name: 连词
item: 连接词或词组以及分句或句子
title: Conjunctions linking words or clauses
explanation: These can join single words, phrases or whole clauses. 加之 (jiāzhī, in addition), 乃至 (nǎizhì, and even, going up to a more extreme item) and 且 (qiě, moreover / and).

name: 助词
title: Sentence-final particles 罢了, 也罢 and 矣
explanation: 罢了 (bàle, that's all / nothing more) goes at the end of a sentence to play something down. 也罢 (yěbà, fine / whether or not) shows reluctant acceptance or indifference, and is often repeated in the form "X 也罢, Y 也罢" meaning "whether X or Y". 知 is not used here; 矣 (yǐ, already / a completed change) is a classical-style sentence-final particle that marks a new situation.

name: 助词
title: The 'like it or not' pattern 爱A不A
explanation: Pattern: 爱 (ài, to like) + verb + 不 (bù, not) + the same verb. It means "do it or don't, I don't care", showing the speaker is indifferent or unwilling to persuade.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 半A半B
explanation: Pattern: 半 (bàn, half) + A + 半 + B. It describes something that is partly A and partly B, with A and B usually being one-character words.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 不A不B
explanation: Pattern: 不 (bù, not) + A + 不 + B. It usually means "neither A nor B", where A and B are often opposites, so the whole describes a middle or awkward in-between state.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 不A而B
explanation: Pattern: 不 (bù, not) + A + 而 (ér, and yet) + B. It means B happens without A being done first, or even though A did not happen.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 东A西B
explanation: Pattern: 东 (dōng, east) + A + 西 (xī, west) + B. It describes actions or things scattered in different places or without a fixed order, like "A here, B there".

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character phrases built on "neither A nor B" (非A非B)
explanation: The fixed pattern 非 (fēi, not, un-) + A + 非 (fēi, not, un-) + B forms a four-character phrase meaning "neither A nor B", where A and B are usually one-character words, often opposites or near-opposites. It often describes something that fits no ordinary category, or is an awkward in-between, as in 非驴非马 (fēi lǘ fēi mǎ, neither donkey nor horse, a hybrid that is neither one thing nor the other).

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 忽A忽B
explanation: This pattern is 忽 (hū, suddenly, now) + A + 忽 (hū) + B, where A and B are usually opposite verbs or adjectives. It means 'now A, now B' and describes something that keeps switching quickly between two states.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 或A或B
explanation: This pattern is 或 (huò, or, either) + A + 或 (huò) + B. It presents two alternatives, 'either A or B', and the A and B parts are often a matched pair of words.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 可A可B
explanation: This pattern is 可 (kě, can, may) + A + 可 (kě) + B, where A and B are often opposites. It means something 'can be A or B', so either way is acceptable or possible, or it could go either way.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 连A带B
explanation: This pattern is 连 (lián, together with) + A + 带 (dài, to bring along) + B, where A and B are usually two verbs. It means doing A and B together or at the same time, 'A while also B'.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 七A八B
explanation: This pattern is 七 (qī, seven) + A + 八 (bā, eight) + B. The numbers are not literal: they suggest 'many' or 'all over the place', and the phrase often describes something messy, scattered or disorderly. A and B are usually two related words, such as two nouns or two verbs.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 时A时B
explanation: This pattern is 时 (shí, at times) + A + 时 (shí) + B. It means 'at one moment A, at another moment B', describing a state or action that alternates or keeps changing.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 无A不B
explanation: This pattern is 无 (wú, without, no) + A + 不 (bù, not) + B. It is a double negative, 'there is no A that does not B', so it means that every A does B, or that everything is covered.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 无A可B
explanation: This pattern is 无 (wú, without, no) + A + 可 (kě, can) + B, where A is usually a noun and B a verb. It means 'there is no A to B', or 'nothing to B', so there is nothing available to do that action with or about.

name: 固定短语
title: Four-character pattern 自A自B
explanation: This pattern is 自 (zì, oneself) + A + 自 (zì) + B, where A and B are usually verbs. It means doing both actions by or to oneself, or in one's own way, such as relying on oneself or acting without regard to others.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 不瞒你说
explanation: 不 (bù, not) + 瞒 (mán, to hide the truth from) + 你 (nǐ, you) + 说 (shuō, to say) literally means 'not hiding it from you, I say'. Speakers use it to introduce a frank admission or a private truth, like 'to be honest' or 'I'll be upfront with you'.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 不是
explanation: 不是 (bú shì, literally 'is not') can open a reply to interrupt, object or show confusion, like 'wait, no' or 'hang on, that's not it'. It signals that the speaker doesn't accept or understand what was just said and is about to correct or question it.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 不是我说你
explanation: 不是 (bú shì, is not) + 我 (wǒ, I) + 说 (shuō, to say, here to criticize) + 你 (nǐ, you) literally means 'it's not that I'm criticizing you'. It softens a coming complaint or piece of advice, like 'I hate to say this, but you...'.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 反过来（说）
explanation: 反过来 (fǎnguòlái, turning around to the opposite) is optionally followed by 说 (shuō, to say). It means 'conversely' or 'looking at it the other way round', and it introduces the opposite side or reversed viewpoint of what was just said.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 概括来说
explanation: 概括 (gàikuò, to summarize) + 来说 (láishuō, speaking from the angle of) means 'to sum up' or 'in general terms'. It introduces a brief summary of the points just made.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 归根到底
explanation: 归根到底 (guī gēn dào dǐ) literally means 'return to the root, reach the bottom'. It means 'in the final analysis' or 'when all is said and done', and it introduces the basic reason or ultimate conclusion.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 话是这么说
explanation: 话 (huà, words, what's said) + 是 (shì, is) + 这么 (zhème, like this) + 说 (shuō, to say) means 'that's how the saying goes' or 'that's true as far as it goes'. The speaker concedes a point and usually follows with a 'but' that raises a difficulty or exception.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 话（又）说回来
explanation: 话 (huà, words, talk) + 又 (yòu, again, optional) + 说 (shuō, to say) + 回来 (huílái, to come back) literally means 'talk coming back around'. It means 'then again' or 'having said that', and it either returns to the main topic or adds a point that balances what was just said.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 换句话说
explanation: 换 (huàn, to change) + 句 (jù, sentence) + 话 (huà, words) + 说 (shuō, to say) means 'in other words'. It introduces a restatement or clearer rephrasing of what came before.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 简（而）言之
explanation: 简 (jiǎn, brief) + 而 (ér, and so, optional linking word) + 言 (yán, to speak, formal) + 之 (zhī, it, formal) means 'in short'. It is a rather formal, written-style way to introduce a short summary.

name: 固定短语
title: Agreement response 可不（是嘛）
explanation: 可 (kě, indeed, adds emphasis) + 不 (bù, not), or the full form 可不是嘛 (kě bú shì ma, with 是 shì, is, and 嘛 ma, a particle adding emphasis), is a reply meaning 'you can say that again' or 'exactly'. It shows strong agreement with what the other person just said.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 老实说
explanation: 老实 (lǎoshi, honest) + 说 (shuō, to say) means 'to be honest' or 'frankly'. It introduces a candid opinion or admission.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker （你）还别说
explanation: 你 (nǐ, you, optional) + 还 (hái, even, still) + 别 (bié, don't) + 说 (shuō, to say) literally means 'don't even say'. It is used to admit that something is surprisingly true or turns out to be right, like 'you know, that's actually true' or 'come to think of it'.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 你看你
explanation: 你 (nǐ, you) + 看 (kàn, to look) + 你 (nǐ) literally means 'look at you'. It is used to scold or complain mildly about someone's behavior or condition, sometimes in an affectionate or exasperated way.

name: 固定短语
title: Polite brush-off 说到哪儿去了
explanation: 说 (shuō, to say) + 到 (dào, to, reaching) + 哪儿 (nǎr, where) + 去 (qù, to go) + 了 (le, particle marking a change) literally means 'where has the talk gone?'. It means 'what are you talking about!' or 'don't say that', and it is used to wave off thanks, an apology, praise or a misunderstanding.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 说真的
explanation: 说 (shuō, to say) + 真 (zhēn, true, real) + 的 (de, particle) means 'seriously' or 'to tell the truth'. The speaker uses it to stress sincerity or to move from joking to a serious point.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 退一步说 (conceding a point)
explanation: 退一步说 (tuì yí bù shuō, taking a step back and saying) is a spoken or written signpost meaning even if we concede a point or lower our standard. It comes after a main argument and introduces a weaker, fallback position. Pattern: main claim + 退一步说 + more lenient point.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 无论如何 (in any case)
explanation: 无论如何 (wúlùn rúhé, no matter what or in any case) says that something holds or will happen whatever the circumstances. It usually comes before the verb or at the start of a clause and shows firm determination or a bottom line.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 要（让）我说 (if you ask me)
explanation: 要（让）我说 (yào ràng wǒ shuō, if you let me say; the 让 (ràng, let) is optional) introduces the speaker's personal opinion. Pattern: 要（让）我说 + the speaker's view.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 这不 (see, look)
explanation: 这不 (zhè bù) here does not mean this is not. It is a spoken opener meaning look or see, pointing out that something just happened or is plainly visible, and it is followed by a clause that states the fact or result.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 这样一来 (as a result)
explanation: 这样一来 (zhèyàng yì lái, this way, then) introduces what follows from the situation just described. Pattern: situation + 这样一来 + consequence.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 真是的 (for goodness' sake)
explanation: 真是的 (zhēnshi de, really now) is a spoken exclamation of mild annoyance or complaint, aimed at a person or a situation. It often stands alone as a short comment, and the speaker is grumbling rather than angry.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 综上所述 (in summary)
explanation: 综上所述 (zōng shàng suǒ shù, taking together what was said above) is a formal phrase that introduces a conclusion drawn from the preceding discussion. It is common in essays and reports. Pattern: 综上所述 + conclusion.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 总的来说 (overall)
explanation: 总的来说 (zǒng de lái shuō, generally speaking) introduces a general summary or overall judgment, after details or mixed points have been given. Pattern: 总的来说 + overall conclusion.

name: 固定短语
title: Discourse marker 总而言之 (in short)
explanation: 总而言之 (zǒng ér yán zhī, in a word or in short) wraps up what came before with a brief closing statement. It is a bit more formal and written-sounding, and it signals that the main point follows.

title: Pattern X到这个地步/份上 (to such a point)
explanation: Pattern: verb or adjective + 到 (dào, reach) + 这个 (zhège, this) 地步 (dìbù, stage or extent) / 份上 (fènshang, point). It means to such an extent or has reached this point, and usually carries surprise, regret or complaint about how far things have gone.

title: Pattern X得要命/要死 (extremely X)
explanation: Pattern: adjective or verb + 得 (de, a particle linking a word to its degree) + 要命 (yàomìng, deadly) / 要死 (yàosǐ, to death). It is a colloquial way to say extremely or terribly, and it is often used for unpleasant states like tired, hot or hungry.

title: Pattern X都不/没X (not even X)
explanation: Pattern: the same verb twice, with 都 (dōu, even) and a negative between them: verb + 都 + 不 (bù, not) / 没 (méi, did not) + verb. It means does not even do X, stressing a complete lack of effort or reaction. 不 is used for habit or willingness, and 没 for something that did not happen.

title: Pattern X就X个Y (do X thoroughly)
explanation: Pattern: verb + 就 (jiù, then) + the same verb + 个 (gè, a linking particle here) + Y. It means if you are going to do X, do it all the way, where Y is a word for the result or extent, such as fully or to one's satisfaction.

title: Pattern X了Y，Y了X (back and forth)
explanation: Pattern: X + 了 (le, marks a completed action) + Y, Y + 了 + X. Two words, often verbs or opposites, swap places in turn to show something going back and forth again and again, or an unresolved cycle.

title: Pattern X也好，Y也罢 (whether X or Y)
explanation: Pattern: X + 也好 (yě hǎo, be it) , Y + 也罢 (yě bà, or be it) , + a conclusion. It means whether X or Y, and the conclusion holds either way, often with 都 (dōu, all) or 总 (zǒng, always).

title: Pattern 别提（有）多……了 (you can't imagine how...)
explanation: Pattern: 别提 (bié tí, don't mention) + 有 (yǒu, have, optional) + 多 (duō, how) + adjective + 了 (le, sentence-final particle). It is an exclamation meaning you can't imagine how adjective it is, or it is extremely adjective.

title: Pattern 不亚于…… (no less than)
explanation: Pattern: A + 不亚于 (bú yà yú, is not inferior to) + B. It says A is at least as good, as great or as serious as B, and often even a bit more. It is somewhat formal.

title: Pattern 不知X是/才好 (not knowing what to do)
explanation: Pattern: subject + 不知 (bù zhī, not know) + question word or phrase, such as 如何 (rúhé, how) or 怎么 (zěnme, how) + 是 (shì) / 才 (cái) + 好 (hǎo, good). It expresses being at a loss about what to do or how to react.

title: Pattern 动不动就…… (at the slightest thing)
explanation: Pattern: subject + 动不动 (dòngbudòng, at every turn) + 就 (jiù, then) + verb phrase. It describes someone doing something too easily or too often, over the slightest cause, and it usually carries a complaint.

title: Pattern verb + 得个…… (verb until the result)
explanation: Pattern: verb + 得 (de, a particle linking a verb to its result) + 个 (gè, a linking particle here) + result phrase. It is a colloquial way to stress a vivid result or extreme degree of an action, as in done until it ends up like this.

title: Pattern verb + 个X (verb to the full)
explanation: Pattern: verb + 个 (gè) + X, where X is a short complement. Here 个 does not count anything; it links the verb to a word showing the result or extent, such as doing something fully or to one's heart's content. It can also make an action sound casual or quick.

title: Pattern 该X（就）X，该Y（就）Y (do what you should)
explanation: Pattern: 该 (gāi, should) + verb X + 就 (jiù, then, optional) + the same verb X, 该 + verb Y + 就 + the same verb Y. It means when it is time to do X, do X, and when it is time to do Y, do Y, which is to carry on as you should without fuss.

title: Pattern 何至于…… (is there any need to go so far?)
explanation: Pattern: subject + 何 (hé, how) 至于 (zhìyú, go so far as to) + verb phrase. It is a rhetorical question meaning there is no need to go as far as that, and it suggests the reaction is exaggerated. It sounds somewhat literary.

title: Pattern 仅次于X (second only to X)
explanation: Pattern: A + 仅 (jǐn, only) 次于 (cìyú, rank next to) + B. It means A ranks right below B, second only to B, and it is used when comparing size, importance or quantity.

title: Pattern 看在X的面子上 (for X's sake)
explanation: Pattern: 看 (kàn, look) 在 (zài, at) + person + 的 (de) 面子 (miànzi, face, meaning respect or reputation) 上 (shàng, on) + request or action. It means out of respect for X, or as a favor to X, and it introduces something done or asked that would not otherwise happen.

title: 没什么……头儿: nothing worth doing
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 没什么 (méi shénme, nothing much) + verb + 头儿 (tóur, worth/appeal). It says there is nothing worth doing or no appeal in doing that verb. 头儿 here is a suffix meaning 'worth' and has nothing to do with 'head'.

title: 没什么好……的: nothing to (do)
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 没什么 (méi shénme, nothing much) + 好 (hǎo, good to/worth) + verb + 的 (de, sentence-ending particle). It means there is nothing worth doing or no reason to do the verb, and it is often used to wave something off.

title: 莫过于: nothing is more than
explanation: 莫过于 (mò guò yú, nothing surpasses) names the greatest or most extreme example of something. Pattern: Statement about a topic + 莫过于 + the thing that tops it. It is formal and means 'nothing is more … than …'.

title: 你说你一个X: scolding someone for not living up to a role
explanation: Pattern: 你说你 (nǐ shuō nǐ, you say you …) + 一个 (yí ge, a/one) + role or identity X + clause. The speaker is complaining that the listener's behavior does not fit that role. It sounds like 'you, being a …, how could you …!'

title: 什么A的B的: vague list of examples
explanation: Pattern: 什么 (shénme, what/whatever) + A + 的 (de, particle) + 什么 + B + 的. A and B are example items, so the phrase means 'things like A and B and so on'. It is casual and often dismissive, or it lumps loose details together.

title: 视……而定: depends on
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 视 (shì, look at/according to) + factor + 而定 (ér dìng, be decided). It means the outcome depends on or is decided by that factor. It is formal and common in announcements and written text.

title: 谈何……: how could one speak of
explanation: Pattern: 谈何 (tán hé, how can one talk of) + noun or verb phrase. It is a rhetorical question meaning that the thing is far from true or possible. 何 (hé) is a formal word for 'what/how'.

content: 无非/不过/只是……罢了/而已
title: 无非/不过/只是……罢了/而已: nothing more than
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 无非 (wúfēi, nothing but) / 不过 (búguò, only) / 只是 (zhǐshì, merely) + content + 罢了 (bà le, that's all) / 而已 (éryǐ, that's all). The two parts work together to play something down, as in 'it is just …, nothing more'. Pick one word from each group.

title: 想X之所想，急X之所急: share others' thoughts and worries
explanation: Pattern: 想 (xiǎng, think) + X + 之所想 (zhī suǒ xiǎng, what X thinks), 急 (jí, be anxious) + X + 之所急 (zhī suǒ jí, what X is anxious about). X is a person or group. It means to think what they think and worry about what they worry about, that is, to put yourself in their place and attend to their needs.

title: 向……致以……: extend greetings or thanks to
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 向 (xiàng, to/toward) + person + 致以 (zhìyǐ, extend/convey) + noun such as thanks, greetings or respect. It is a formal way of saying someone expresses something to someone else, and it is common in speeches and letters.

title: 要X有/没X，要Y有/没Y: has (or lacks) everything
explanation: Pattern: 要 (yào, if it comes to) + X + 有 (yǒu, have) + X, 要 + Y + 有 + Y; or the same with 没 (méi, not have). X and Y repeat the same word on both sides of 有/没. With 有 it means the subject has everything needed, whether X or Y. With 没 it means the subject has neither.

title: 因……而……: because of … hence
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 因 (yīn, because of) + cause + 而 (ér, and so/thus) + result. It links a cause to its result in a formal, compact way, as in 'because of …, therefore …'.

title: 有何X: what X is there
explanation: Pattern: 有 (yǒu, have/there is) + 何 (hé, what) + noun X. It is a formal question meaning 'what X is there?' and is often rhetorical, implying that there is none.

title: 有什么……头儿: what is worth doing (rhetorical)
explanation: Pattern: 有什么 (yǒu shénme, what is there) + verb + 头儿 (tóur, worth/appeal). It is a rhetorical question meaning that doing the verb is not worth it. It carries the same sense as 没什么……头儿 but is phrased as a question.

title: （在）……之余: in the time left over from
explanation: Pattern: (在 (zài, at/in)) + activity + 之余 (zhī yú, in the time left over/besides) + another action. It means that besides or after the main activity, the subject also does something else. 在 is optional.

title: 值此……之际: on the occasion of
explanation: Pattern: 值此 (zhí cǐ, on this occasion of) + event or time + 之际 (zhījì, at the time of), + main clause. It is a formal opening for speeches, greetings and announcements that marks a special moment.

name: 特殊句型
title: Comparing with 于 or 过
explanation: Pattern: A + adjective + 于 (yú, than) + B, or A + adjective + 过 (guò, surpass) + B. Both mean A is more … than B. They are more formal or literary than the usual 比 (bǐ, than) comparison.

name: 简单复句
title: 一来……，二来……，三来……: listing reasons (spoken)
explanation: 一来 (yī lái, for one thing), 二来 (èr lái, for another), 三来 (sān lái, third) introduce reasons or points one after another. Each part is followed by its own reason, and often only the first two parts appear.

name: 简单复句
title: 一则……，二则……，三则……: listing reasons (formal)
explanation: 一则 (yī zé, for one thing), 二则 (èr zé, for another), 三则 (sān zé, third) introduce reasons or points in order. It means the same as 一来……二来……, but it sounds more formal and written.

name: 简单复句
title: 所谓……，就是……: defining a term
explanation: Pattern: 所谓 (suǒ wèi, what is called/so-called) + term, 就是 (jiù shì, is) + explanation. The first part names a concept and the second part explains what it means.

name: 简单复句
title: 或……，或……: either/or, or now … now
explanation: Pattern: 或 (huò, or) + option A, 或 + option B. It presents alternatives, or it lists different things that people or things do, as in 'some do …, some do …' or 'now … now …'.

name: 简单复句
title: 宁可/宁愿……，也不……: would rather … than
explanation: Pattern: Subject + 宁可 (nìngkě, would rather) / 宁愿 (nìngyuàn, would rather) + preferred option, 也不 (yě bù, still would not) + rejected option. The first part is what the speaker chooses, even if it is hard, and the second part is what they refuse.

name: 简单复句
title: 与其……，宁愿/宁可……: rather than … better to
explanation: Pattern: 与其 (yǔqí, rather than) + rejected option, 宁愿 (nìngyuàn, would rather) / 宁可 (nìngkě, would rather) + preferred option. Compared with 宁可……也不……, the rejected choice comes first here and the preferred one second.

name: 简单复句
title: X（倒）是X（了），……: admitting a point, then contrasting
explanation: Pattern: X + (倒 (dào, indeed/admittedly)) + 是 (shì, is) + X (+ 了 (le, particle marking a completed change)), + contrasting clause. X is the same word repeated, such as a verb or adjective. The speaker concedes that it is true, but the next clause turns to a problem or an opposing point, as in 'it is X, but …'.

name: 简单复句
title: 别看……，……: don't be fooled by appearances
explanation: Pattern: 别看 (bié kàn, don't look at/although it looks) + apparent situation, + clause that contrasts with it. It means that something looks one way but the reality is different, as in 'although it seems …, actually …'.

name: 简单复句
title: Although... but... (虽说)
