explanation: Pattern: 虽说 (suī shuō, although) + clause 1, + 但 (dàn, but) / 可 (kě, but) + clause 2. The first clause admits a fact, and the second clause, introduced by either 但 or 可, says something that pulls in the opposite direction.

name: 简单复句
title: No matter whether... or not
explanation: Pattern: 无论 (wúlùn, no matter) + thing + 与否 (yǔfǒu, or not), + 都 (dōu, all the same) + result. It says the result stays the same whether or not the thing happens or is true, and it is mostly found in written Chinese.

name: 简单复句
title: Anyone who... all can... (formal)
explanation: Pattern: 凡 (fán, every, any) + group or condition + (者 zhě, the one who), + 均 (jūn, all, without exception) + (可 kě, may) + result. It states a rule that applies to everyone or everything meeting the condition, in formal writing.

name: 简单复句
title: If... (formal 假若/假使)
explanation: Pattern: 假若 (jiǎruò, if) / 假使 (jiǎshǐ, if) + supposed situation, + result. Both words mean 'if' and are more formal than everyday words for 'if'. The first clause sets up a hypothetical and the second says what follows.

name: 简单复句
title: Luckily... otherwise...
explanation: Pattern: 幸亏 (xìngkuī, luckily) / 幸好 (xìnghǎo, luckily) + fortunate fact, + 不然 (bùrán, otherwise) / 否则 (fǒuzé, otherwise) + bad outcome. The first clause names what saved the situation, and the second says what would have happened without it.

name: 简单复句
title: Even if... still...
explanation: Pattern: 纵然 (zòngrán, even if) / 纵使 (zòngshǐ, even if) + supposed situation, + subject + 也 (yě, still) + result. Even in that extreme or unfavorable case, the result does not change. It is a formal, written style.

name: 简单复句
title: Because... therefore... (formal)
explanation: Pattern: (因 yīn, because) + reason, + 故 (gù, therefore) + result. This is the formal written version of cause and effect, and the 因 at the start may be left out, so look for 故 introducing the result.

name: 简单复句
title: ...so much so that...
explanation: Pattern: Cause or situation, + 以至 (yǐzhì, so much so that) / 以至于 (yǐzhìyú, so much so that) + result. The second part is a consequence that is often extreme or unexpected, and 以至于 means the same as 以至.

name: 简单复句
title: Let alone... even...
explanation: Pattern: 别说 (bié shuō, let alone, not to mention) + bigger case, + 都 (dōu, even) / 也 (yě, even) + smaller case. If even the smaller case is true or untrue, the bigger case obviously is too, so it need not be discussed.

name: 简单复句
title: Not to mention X, but also Y
explanation: Pattern: Clause 1 + 不说 (bù shuō, not to mention, setting aside), + 还 (hái, also, on top of that) + clause 2. The first thing is already bad or notable, and the second adds a further point, often one that is worse.

name: 简单复句
title: Even X..., needless to say Y
explanation: Pattern: 连 (lián, even) + minor case + 都 (dōu, even) + …, + 更 (gèng, even more) + 不用说 (bú yòng shuō, needless to say) + bigger case + 了 (le, sentence-ending particle). If even the easy or small case holds, the harder or larger case certainly does.

name: 简单复句
title: Even X..., let alone Y
explanation: Pattern: X + 尚且 (shàngqiě, even) + …, + (更 gèng, even more) + 何况 (hékuàng, let alone, how much more) + Y. If even the easier case X is a certain way, the harder case Y must be so all the more. It is formal in tone.

name: 简单复句
title: ..., needless to say...
explanation: Pattern: Statement, + 更 (gèng, even more) + 不用说 (bú yòng shuō, needless to say) + further case + 了 (le, sentence-ending particle). After stating one case, it adds that a bigger or more obvious case goes without saying.

name: 简单复句
title: For the sake of... (为了...起见)
explanation: Pattern: 为 (wèi, for) + (了 le, particle) + concern + 起见 (qǐjiàn, for the sake of), + action. The part between 为 and 起见 gives the concern, such as safety or convenience, and the action follows after the comma.

name: 简单复句
title: ..., in order to... (以)
explanation: Pattern: Action, + 以 (yǐ, in order to, so as to) + purpose. The purpose comes after the action, which is the reverse of the order with 为了 (wèile, in order to). It is a formal, written pattern.

name: 简单复句
title: Must... in order to...
explanation: Pattern: 非得 (fēiděi, must, have to) + condition + 才 (cái, only then) + result. It says the result happens only if the condition is met. It is a tight sentence with no comma between the two halves.

name: 简单复句
title: No matter... still...
explanation: Pattern: 任 (rèn, no matter, however) + whoever or whatever + 也 (yě, still) + result. Whatever someone says or does, the result stays the same. It is a tight sentence, often with no comma between the two halves.

name: 多重复句
title: Multi-level sentences with side-by-side ideas
explanation: A long sentence built in layers, where at least one layer lists ideas of equal standing next to each other. Look at the punctuation: the biggest break, often a semicolon, splits the sentence first, and the smaller commas split each part further.

name: 多重复句
title: Multi-level sentences with contrast
explanation: A long sentence in layers where at least one layer has a 'but' relationship, with the second idea going against the first. Find the biggest break first, often marked by a semicolon, then work out how the smaller parts connect inside each side.

name: 多重复句
title: Multi-level sentences with 'if' situations
explanation: A long sentence in layers where at least one layer is an 'if... then...' relationship. Work out the big split first, then see which part sets up the supposed situation and which part gives the result.

name: 多重复句
title: Multi-level sentences with cause and effect
explanation: A long sentence in layers where at least one layer links a reason to its result. Find the main break first, often at a semicolon, then see where the reasons and results sit inside each part.

name: 多重复句
title: Multi-level sentences with 'and even further' steps
explanation: A long sentence in layers where at least one layer moves one step further, with the later idea stronger or broader than the earlier one. Split the sentence at its biggest break first, then check how the smaller parts build on each other.

title: Passages ordered by time
explanation: A group of sentences arranged in the order events happened, such as morning to evening or past to future. Time words and phrases mark the steps, and reading them in order shows how the story moves along.

title: Passages ordered by space
explanation: A group of sentences arranged by location, such as moving from outside to inside, near to far, or one place to the next. Words for places and directions mark each step, and together they build a picture of the scene.

title: Passages ordered by logic
explanation: A group of sentences arranged by reasoning rather than by time or place, such as general to specific, problem to solution, or cause to effect. Each sentence follows from the one before, and linking words signal the steps.

title: Extending the topic
explanation: A group of sentences keeps the same topic and adds more detail, so each new sentence builds on what the previous one said about it. When reading, look for the later sentences giving further information, explanation or description of the same thing instead of introducing something new.

title: Switching the topic
explanation: Within a passage, the sentences move from one topic to a different one, often marked by a new subject or a new thing being talked about. When reading, notice where the subject changes so you do not assume the new sentence is still about the earlier topic.

title: Omitting a repeated element that came earlier
explanation: A subject, object or other part already mentioned in an earlier sentence is left out of the following sentence because it is clear from context. When a sentence seems to lack a subject or object, look back to the previous sentence to fill in who or what it refers to.

title: Omitting an element that is stated later
explanation: A subject or other part is left out in the first sentence and only appears in a later sentence that follows. When an opening sentence seems to lack a subject or object, read ahead to find the word that supplies it.
